rules.rule: A person moving to Tennessee must apply for a Tennessee driver license if they live in Tennessee longer than 30 days, work in Tennessee, or would qualify as a registered Tennessee voter.
rules.quote: live in Tennessee longer than 30 days OR • are working in Tennessee OR • would otherwise qualify as a registered Tennessee voter.

rules.rule: A Class D license is required to operate any vehicle up to a maximum weight of 26,000 pounds.
rules.quote: A Class D license is required to operate any vehicle, up to a maximum weight of 26,000 pounds.

rules.rule: A vehicle under 26,000 pounds still requires a Class C license if it hauls hazardous materials, carries 16 or more passengers including the driver, or is used as a school bus.
rules.quote: Vehicles that are under 26,000 pounds cannot be operated with a Class D license if the vehicle is (a) transporting hazardous materials, (b) transporting sixteen (16 or more passengers (including the driver), or (c) used as a school bus.

rules.rule: To qualify for a Class D license you must be at least 16 and pass a vision screening, knowledge test and driving test.
rules.quote: To qualify for a Class D license, you must be at least 16 years of age, and must pass a vision screening, knowledge test, and driving test.

rules.rule: A For-Hire endorsement is required when a person's main job is to drive or transport persons or property in a Class D vehicle.
rules.quote: If a person's main job is to drive or transport persons, or transport property in a Class D vehicle, a For Hire endorsement must be added to the Class D license.

rules.rule: For-Hire applicants must generally be at least 18 and have 2 years of unrestricted driving experience.
rules.quote: They have 2 years of unrestricted driving experience.
extraQuotes: They are at least 18 years of age

rules.rule: Off-road vehicles and ATVs may not be driven on Tennessee or federal highways and may cross roadways only at ninety-degree angles.
rules.quote: "off-road" motor vehicles or All-terrain Vehicles (ATVs) may not be driven on any Tennessee/Federal highways/interstate roads. Legally this type of vehicle can only cross roadways by taking ninety-degree (90 degree) angles and must not directly cross any road/highway/interstate.

rules.rule: Vehicles weighing 26,001 or more pounds require a Commercial Driver License.
rules.quote: Operators of larger and more complex vehicles weighing 26,001 or more pounds will need to apply for a Commercial Driver License (CDL).

rules.rule: A Class PD learner permit requires the applicant to be 15 and to pass the written knowledge test and vision screening.
rules.quote: To obtain a Class PD license, you must have reached the age of 15 and pass the written knowledge test and vision screening for a class D license.

rules.rule: A Class PD holder may drive only when accompanied by a licensed driver at least 21 years old sitting in the seat beside the driver.
rules.quote: A driver with a Class PD license may operate an automobile only when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old and is sitting in the seat beside the driver.

rules.rule: A PD holder need not repeat the knowledge test when applying for an Intermediate Class D unless the permit expired more than 12 months before the skills test.
rules.quote: they do not need to repeat the knowledge test unless the license permit expired more than 12 months prior to the driving skills test.

rules.rule: A Class H hardship license may be issued to a minor who is 14 years old, only in cases of family hardship, and it is valid only for daylight hours and travel to authorized locations.
rules.quote: The Class H license is valid only for daylight hours and for travel to authorized locations as specified in the approval letter.
extraQuotes: A hardship license (Class H) may be issued to a minor who is 14 years old

rules.rule: A hardship license expires when the applicant reaches age 16, regardless of age at approval.
rules.quote: Regardless of age at time of approval, a Hardship License will expire when the applicant reaches the age of 16.

rules.rule: You must have your driver license in your possession while driving and show it on request; not having it is a Class D misdemeanor fined not less than $2.00 and no more than $50.00.
rules.quote: It is a Class D misdemeanor. If you do not have your license with you, you may be fined not less than two dollars ($2.00) and no more than fifty dollars ($50.00).

rules.rule: Driving while revoked, canceled or suspended is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by a fine up to $1,000 and/or six months in jail.
rules.quote: Driving while revoked, canceled, or suspended is a class B misdemeanor. The penalty is a fine up to one-thousand dollars ($1,000) and/or six months in jail.

rules.rule: Non-U.S. citizens in managerial or technical employment may drive on a foreign/out-of-state license for 6 months and must then apply for a Tennessee license.
rules.quote: may operate vehicles with a valid driver license issued by another state, country, or international body for a period of 6 months. These individuals must apply for a Tennessee license at the end of 6 months.

rules.rule: A person whose license is currently suspended or revoked in this or any other state is not eligible for a Tennessee license.
rules.quote: Anyone whose license is currently suspended or revoked in this, or any other state.

rules.rule: Anyone under 18 who has dropped out of school before graduating, or who does not make satisfactory progress, is not eligible for a license.
rules.quote: Anyone under the age of 18, who has dropped out of school before graduating, or who does not make "satisfactory progress" in school.

rules.rule: Minors between 13 and 17 who have a license, permit or state ID may choose to register as an organ donor.
rules.quote: Minors who are between the ages of 13 and 17 years old, and who have driver's license, permit or state ID can choose to register as a donor, according to the Tennessee Uniform Anatomical Gifts Act.

rules.rule: An International Driving Permit is not valid by itself for driving in the United States and must be carried with the driver's regular valid U.S. license.
rules.quote: The IDP is NOT valid for driving in the United States or its territories and it is NOT valid by itself for driving. • The IDP MUST be carried with the driver's regular valid U.S. Driver License.

rules.rule: To obtain an IDP a United States citizen must be at least eighteen years of age, and the IDP is valid for one year only from the date of issuance.
rules.quote: The IDP is valid for one (1) year only from the date of issuance
extraQuotes: Be at least eighteen (18) years of age

rules.rule: A registered sexual offender or violent sexual offender must always have their driver license, photo identification card or identification certificate in their possession.
rules.quote: Sexual Offender and Violent Sexual Offenders shall always have their driver license, photo identification card or identification certificate in their possession.

rules.rule: The examiner requires two items of proof of identity, and original applicants must have at least one item from the Primary Identification list.
rules.quote: ORIGINAL applicants must have at least one item from the Primary Identification list. The second item may be from the Secondary Identification list or another item from the Primary Identification list.

rules.rule: Proof of residency requires two documents, current within the last 4 months, showing the Tennessee residence address — no P.O. boxes.
rules.quote: TWO PROOFS OF TENNESSEE RESIDENCY WITH YOUR NAME AND RESIDENT ADDRESS – NO P.O. BOXES (CURRENT=FROM LAST 4 MONTHS)

rules.rule: All documents must be originals or certified; no photocopies or faxes are accepted.
rules.quote: IMPORTANT: All Documents Must be Originals or Certified. No Faxes or Photocopies.

rules.rule: As of January 1, 2016, Tennessee licenses for persons over 21 expire every eight years from the date of issuance.
rules.quote: As of January 1, 2016, Tennessee licenses for persons over the age of 21 expire every eight years from the date of issuance.

rules.rule: New or returning residents must obtain a Tennessee driver license no later than thirty days after establishing residency.
rules.quote: must obtain a Tennessee driver license no later than thirty (30) days after establishing residency.

rules.rule: New or returning residents whose out-of-state license has been expired more than six months must take the knowledge exam, road skills test and vision screening.
rules.quote: New or returning residents whose out of state license has been expired for more than six months must take the Tennessee knowledge exam, road skills test, and vision screening.

rules.rule: Discharged or reassigned military personnel must renew their license within sixty days of separation or reassignment to Tennessee.
rules.quote: he or she must renew his/her license within sixty (60) days following the date of separation on the DD214 form or reassignment to Tennessee.

rules.rule: A license expired more than 30 calendar days carries a $5.00 late fee; after six months the late fee doubles to $10.00.
rules.quote: If your license has expired more than thirty (30) calendar days, there will be a five-dollar ($5.00) late fee. After six (6) months, the late fee doubles to $10.00.

rules.rule: If five years pass without renewing, the driver must pay the $10.00 late fee and pass the vision screening, knowledge and skills tests.
rules.quote: If you let five (5) years go by without renewing, not only will you have to pay the $10.00 late fee, you will also have to pass the vision screening, knowledge, and skills test.

rules.rule: There is no grace period; when your license expires you are no longer entitled to drive and are subject to the same penalties as someone never licensed.
rules.quote: These are no "grace periods." When your license expires, you are no longer entitled to drive a vehicle or motorcycle and will be subject to the same penalties as someone who has never been licensed.

rules.rule: State law requires notifying the Department of Safety within ten days of any residence address change, even if you did not physically move.
rules.quote: you are required by state law to notify the Department of Safety within ten (10) days of this change.

rules.rule: By law your license must show a legal residential address; a post office box alone will not be accepted.
rules.quote: by law, your license must show your legal residential address: a house, and/or apartment number and the street, road or highway
extraQuotes: A post office box alone will not be accepted as a residential address.

rules.rule: The GDL law does not apply to anyone age 18 or older, or to those under 18 who have graduated high school or received a GED.
rules.quote: No. The GDL law does not apply to anyone age 18 or older or to those persons under 18 who have graduated high school or received a GED.

rules.rule: There are four steps to a full unrestricted license: Learner Permit, Intermediate Restricted License, Intermediate Unrestricted License, and Regular Driver License.
rules.quote: There are four steps to becoming a full, unrestricted Driver License holder: 1. Learner Permit 2. Intermediate Restricted License 3. Intermediate Unrestricted License 4. Regular Driver License.

rules.rule: A license issued under the first three GDL steps has "GDL" printed in the bottom left corner.
rules.quote: A license issued under the first three steps will have "GDL" printed in the bottom left corner.

rules.rule: The learner permit requires you to be 15 years old and to pass the standard written exams and vision screening.
rules.quote: You must be 15 years old and pass the standard written exams and vision screening.

rules.rule: You must hold a learner permit for 180 days to move to the Intermediate Restricted License step.
rules.quote: You must hold a learner permit for 180 days in order to move to the Intermediate Restricted License step.

rules.rule: A learner permit holder may drive a car only when accompanied by a licensed driver 21 years or older riding in the front seat.
rules.quote: You may drive a car only when accompanied by a licensed driver 21 years or older who is riding in the front seat of the vehicle.

rules.rule: A learner permit holder may not drive between the hours of 10 P.M. and 6 A.M.
rules.quote: You may not drive between the hours of 10 P.M. and 6 A.M.

rules.rule: The driver and all passengers must wear a safety belt when driving on a learner permit.
rules.quote: Driver and passengers must wear a safety belt.

rules.rule: The Intermediate Restricted License requires you to be 16 years old and to pass the driving skills test (road test).
rules.quote: You must be 16 years old and pass the driving skills test, also known as the road test.

rules.rule: You cannot have moving-violation convictions or contributed accidents equaling 6 or more points within a 12-month period to move to Intermediate Restricted.
rules.quote: You cannot have been convicted of moving violations or contributed to accidents that equal to 6 or more points within a 12 month period.

rules.rule: The Intermediate Restricted License requires certified verification of fifty hours of driving experience, ten of them at night, on form SF-1256.
rules.quote: You must have verification from a parent, legal guardian or licensed driving instructor stating you have completed fifty hours (ten hours at night) of driving experience. Certification of driving experience must be made on the official form (SF-1256)

rules.rule: An Intermediate Restricted License holder is prohibited from driving between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m. unless an enumerated exception applies.
rules.quote: Those with an Intermediate Restricted License are prohibited from driving between the hours of 11 p.m. and 6 a.m. UNLESS the meet one of the following circumstances

rules.rule: An Intermediate Restricted License holder may have only 1 other passenger in the vehicle, unless an exception applies.
rules.quote: Those with an intermediate license can only have 1 other passenger in the vehicle. UNLESS: • One or more of the passengers is age 21 or older and has a valid, unrestricted license; OR • The passengers are brothers and sisters, step-brothers or step-sisters, adopted or fostered children residing in the same house as the driver

rules.rule: Curfew exceptions are: accompanied by a parent/guardian; accompanied by a designated licensed driver 21+; to/from a school-sponsored activity with written permission; to/from work with written permission; or to/from hunting or fishing between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. with a valid license.
rules.quote: They are driving to or from hunting or fishing between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. and have in their possession a valid hunting or fishing license.

rules.rule: The Intermediate Unrestricted License requires you to be 17 years old.
rules.quote: To apply for the Intermediate Unrestricted from the Intermediate Restricted License, you must be 17 years old

rules.rule: You must have held the Intermediate Restricted License for 1 year to move to Intermediate Unrestricted.
rules.quote: You must have held an Intermediate Restricted License for 1 year.

rules.rule: Six or more points, contributing to a traffic crash, or a second seatbelt-violation conviction makes a teen ineligible for the Unrestricted Intermediate License for an additional ninety days beyond the minimum one year.
rules.quote: A teen driver will be ineligible for an Unrestricted Intermediate License for additional ninety (90) days beyond the minimum one year if: 1. The driver has received six (6) or more points
extraQuotes: 2. The driver has contributed to a traffic crash, or 3. The driver has been convicted of a second seatbelt violation

rules.rule: A second moving violation while holding the Intermediate Restricted License requires completion of an approved Driver Education class before receiving the Intermediate Unrestricted License.
rules.quote: If the teen driver gets a second moving violation while holding the Intermediate Restricted Driver License, an approved Driver Education class MUST BE COMPLETED before receiving an Intermediate Unrestricted Driver License.

rules.rule: Contributing to the occurrence of a fatal accident while on a learner permit requires the teen to maintain a Learner Permit only until age 18.
rules.quote: Must maintain a Learner Permit only until teen reaches the age of 18

rules.rule: A Class D regular driver license may be obtained at 18, or on graduating high school or receiving a GED, whichever is sooner.
rules.quote: You may obtain a Class D regular driver license when you are 18 years of age, or when you graduate from high school or receive a GED, whichever is sooner.

rules.rule: A 16-year-old emancipated by active duty military service, marriage or court order may obtain a Class D regular driver license.
rules.quote: If you are 16 years of age you may also obtain a Class D regular driver license if you are emancipated by active duty military service, marriage or court order.

rules.rule: Effective July 1, 2018 all licenses issued to persons under 21 years of age are in a vertical format.
rules.quote: Effective July 1, 2018 all licenses issued to persons under 21 years of age are in a vertical format.

rules.rule: Applicants under eighteen must have an adult sign a Minor/Teenage Affidavit and Cancellation form assuming financial responsibility for the minor driver.
rules.quote: Applicants under eighteen years old must have an adult sign a Minor/Teenage Affidavit and Cancellation form
extraQuotes: This includes assuming financial responsibility for the minor driver.

rules.rule: Applicants under 18 must prove they are enrolled in or have graduated from high school, and form SF1010 is valid only 30 days from signing.
rules.quote: This form is only valid for thirty (30) days from the date of signing by the school official.

rules.rule: A student who drops out a second time must wait until age 18 before being eligible to apply for a license again.
rules.quote: The second time a student drops out, he or she must wait to turn eighteen (18) years old before being eligible to apply for a license again.

rules.rule: A student returning to school must pay a $20 reinstatement fee in addition to application and license fees.
rules.quote: The student will be required to pay a $20 reinstatement fee, in addition to the appropriate application and license fees.

rules.rule: Tennessee law prohibits any driver holding a learner permit or intermediate driver license from using a cell phone while driving on any Tennessee roadway.
rules.quote: Tennessee law prohibits any driver possessing a learner permit or intermediate driver license from using a cell phone while driving on any Tennessee roadway.

rules.rule: A teen cell-phone conviction is a Class C misdemeanor with a $50.00 fine, 6 points on the minor's record, and a 90-day delay in eligibility for the Intermediate Restricted Driver License.
rules.quote: Class C misdemeanor • $50.00 fine • 6 points on to a minor's driving record • 90 day delay in eligibility for intermediate Restricted Driver License

rules.rule: A 15-year-old with a valid out-of-state permit qualifies only for a Tennessee learner permit and must hold a valid permit for a total of 180 days and turn 16 before eligibility for Intermediate Restricted.
rules.quote: You must hold a valid learner permit for a total of 180 days and turn sixteen (16) years old before being eligible for the Intermediate Restricted License Class D.

rules.rule: Regardless of how long a license was held in the previous state, a Tennessee Intermediate Restricted license must be held for one year before qualifying for Intermediate Unrestricted.
rules.quote: Regardless of the length of time a license is held in the previous state, a Tennessee Intermediate Restricted license must be held for one year before qualifying for the Intermediate Unrestricted license.

rules.rule: The driver license examination consists of a vision screening, a knowledge test and a road test.
rules.quote: Your driver license examination will consist of a vision screening, a knowledge test, and a road test.

rules.rule: An applicant is required to have at least 20/40 vision in each eye individually and both eyes together, with or without corrective lenses.
rules.quote: An applicant is required to have at least 20/40 vision in each eye individually and both eyes together. This may be with or without your glasses or contact lenses.

rules.rule: The knowledge test is approximately 25% traffic signs and signals, 25% safe driving principles, 25% rules of the road, and 25% drugs and alcohol.
rules.quote: Traffic signs and signals—25% Safe driving principles—25% Rules of the road—25% Drugs and alcohol—25%

rules.rule: By law at least 25 percent of the questions on the knowledge test must deal with driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol.
rules.quote: by law, at least 25 percent of the questions on the knowledge test must consist of questions dealing with this topic.

rules.rule: A mandatory 1-day waiting period is required after failing any driver license knowledge test, and no test may be repeated on the same day.
rules.quote: a mandatory 1-day waiting period is required after failing any driver license knowledge test.
extraQuotes: No test may be repeated on the same day.

rules.rule: Cheating results in automatic failure and the applicant may not re-attempt the test for 30 days.
rules.quote: Any form of cheating by an applicant on a required examination will result in an automatic failure and the applicant will not be allowed to re-attempt the test for 30 days.

rules.rule: A $2 application fee is required each time you take a test and fail.
rules.quote: You will be required to pay the $2 application fee each time you take a test and fail.

rules.rule: If you are more than 5 minutes late for your road test appointment, the test is canceled and must be rescheduled.
rules.quote: If you are more than 5 minutes late for your appointment time, your road skills test will be canceled and you will need to reschedule for a later date.

rules.rule: Road tests are given in light to moderate rain, fog or snow but not in heavy rain, thunderstorms, thick fog, flooded or snow/ice-covered roads, or severe weather warnings.
rules.quote: Road tests will be given in light to moderate rain, fog or snow. However, they will NOT be given in heavy rain, thunderstorms, thick fog cover, when roads are flooded, covered/packed with snow and ice, during severe weather warnings (i.e. tornado)

rules.rule: Road test appointments may be made up to 45 days in advance, and you should arrive at least 15 minutes early.
rules.quote: arrive at the Driver License Service Center at least 15 minutes prior to your scheduled appointment time
extraQuotes: You will be able to make your appointment up to 45 days in advance of your desired test date.

rules.rule: Any passenger motor vehicle manufactured or assembled in 1969 or later must be equipped with safety belts in good usable condition.
rules.quote: Any passenger motor vehicle manufactured or assembled in 1969 or later must be equipped with safety belts and must be in good usable condition for both the applicant and the examiner.

rules.rule: By law all automobiles must have two separate methods of applying brakes — a regular foot brake and a parking brake.
rules.quote: By law all automobiles must have two separate methods of applying brakes. They must have a regular foot brake and a parking brake.

rules.rule: Motor vehicles must be equipped with at least two headlights but no more than four white headlights.
rules.quote: Motor vehicles must be equipped with at least two headlights but no more than four white headlights.

rules.rule: Passenger vehicles must be equipped with a rear license light, two red tail lights, and two red brake lights.
rules.quote: Passenger vehicles must be equipped with a rear license light, two red tail lights, and two red brake lights.

rules.rule: Every vehicle with a windshield should have 2 windshield wipers, unless 1 wiper cleans to within 1 inch of the inside of the windshield.
rules.quote: should have 2 windshield wipers for cleaning rain or any other moisture in order to permit clear vision for the driver, unless 1 wiper cleans to within 1 inch of the inside of the windshield.

rules.rule: The vehicle must have at least one rearview mirror that does not interfere with the driver's view of the rear.
rules.quote: The vehicle must have at least one rearview mirror not interfering with the driver's view of the rear.

rules.rule: A horn is required on all motor vehicles.
rules.quote: A horn is required on all motor vehicles.

rules.rule: No tinting material may be affixed to the windshield of any motor vehicle.
rules.quote: No tinting material may be affixed to the windshield of any motor vehicle.

rules.rule: On a passenger car, no material transmitting less than 35% of visible light may be attached to any window.
rules.quote: Passenger Car. No material which transmits less than 35% of visible light may be attached to any window.

rules.rule: Every vehicle must be equipped with a muffler to prevent excessive or unusual noises and polluting smoke.
rules.quote: Every vehicle must be equipped with a muffler to prevent excessive or unusual noises and polluting smoke.

rules.rule: Both the driver door and the passenger door must open from the inside and the outside.
rules.quote: Both the driver door and the passenger door must open from the inside and the outside.

rules.rule: Passenger cars must have bumpers within 14 to 22 inches from the ground; 4x4 recreational vehicles 14 to 31 inches.
rules.quote: Passenger cars must have bumpers which are within a range of 14 to 22 inches from the ground; 4x4 recreational vehicles must have bumpers with a range of 14 to 31 inches.

rules.rule: Every vehicle must have a working speedometer in order to gauge vehicle speed.
rules.quote: Every vehicle must have a working speedometer in order to gauge vehicle speed.

rules.rule: It is unlawful to drive with a windshield so cracked or covered with steam or frost that clear vision is prevented.
rules.quote: It is unlawful to drive a motor vehicle with a windshield that is so cracked, or covered with steam or frost that clear vision is prevented.

rules.rule: An applicant fails the road test immediately for violating any traffic law, lack of cooperation or refusal to follow directions, any dangerous action, or contributing to an accident.
rules.quote: Violation of any traffic law • Lack of cooperation or refusal to follow directions • Any dangerous action • Contributing to an accident

rules.rule: You must speak and understand enough of the English language to communicate with the Examiner during the road test.
rules.quote: You must speak and understand enough of the English language to communicate with the Examiner during the road test.

rules.rule: Only the applicant and the examiner may be in the vehicle during the driving test, and no animal may be in the vehicle.
rules.quote: The only people allowed in the vehicle are you and the examiner (or other authorized personnel). No animal may be in the vehicle.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Officers can stop and ticket drivers solely for disobeying safety belt and Child Restraint Device laws.
rules.quote: Officers can stop and ticket drivers solely for disobeying Safety belt and Child Restraint Device (CRD) laws.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Safety belts are required for all drivers and all front-seat passengers any time the vehicle is in motion.
rules.quote: Safety belts are required for ALL drivers and all passengers in the FRONT seat, any time the vehicle is in motion.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Safety belts are required for back-seat passengers under 17 years old, and for passengers aged 4 through 17 when the driver holds a learner permit or intermediate license.
rules.quote: If the driver has either a learner permit or an intermediate license, and when the passengers are between four and 17 years old.
extraQuotes: If the passengers are under 17 years old

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: A passenger four through eight years old and shorter than four feet nine inches must be in a child booster seat at all times, in the back seat if the vehicle has one.
rules.quote: If the passenger is four through eight years old and is shorter than four feet, nine inches in height. These passengers must be in a child booster seat at all times. Children in booster seats must be in the back seat of a vehicle, if the vehicle has a back seat.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: A child under one year old, or any child weighing less than 20 pounds, must be in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system.
rules.quote: A child under one year old, or any child weighing less than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system (car seat) that is facing the rear of the car.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Children one through three years old who weigh more than 20 pounds must be in a forward-facing child passenger restraint system.
rules.quote: Children who are one through three years old, and who weigh more than 20 pounds, must be in a child passenger restraint system that is facing forward.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Children four through eight years old under four feet nine inches must be in a belt-positioning booster seat system and wearing a seatbelt.
rules.quote: Children who are four through eight years old and whose height is under four feet, nine inches, must be in a belt positioning booster seat system (child booster car seat) and wearing a seatbelt.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: The driver is responsible for the protection of children up to age sixteen and may be fined $50.00 if children under 16 are not properly restrained.
rules.quote: which makes the driver responsible for their protection up to the age of sixteen (16). If children under age 16 are not properly restrained, the driver may be charged and fined $50.00 for violation of the law.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: If the child's parent or legal guardian is in the car but not driving, the parent or guardian is responsible and may be fined for non-compliance.
rules.quote: If the child's parent or legal guardian is present in the car but not driving, then the parent or legal guardian is responsible for making sure that the child is properly transported and may be fined for non-compliance.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Failing to use a car seat or booster seat for a child under nine or under four feet nine inches can be charged as a Class C misdemeanor with a required class on safely transporting children.
rules.quote: The driver can be charged with a Class C misdemeanor, required to attend a class on safely transporting children and required to pay possible fees and fines.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: The lap belt should be worn low over the pelvis with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs snugly.
rules.quote: The lap belt should be worn low over the pelvis with the bottom edge touching the tops of the thighs snugly.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: The shoulder belt should be worn over the shoulder and across the chest, not under the arm and over the abdomen.
rules.quote: The shoulder belt should be worn over the shoulder and across the chest, not under the arm and over the abdomen.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.
rules.quote: Pregnant women should wear the lap belt below the abdomen and the shoulder belt above the belly.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Children ages 12 and under are safer in the back seat of a vehicle.
rules.quote: CHILDREN ages 12 and under are safer in the back seat of a vehicle.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Ten to twelve inches between the chest and the air bag module is recommended by NHTSA.
rules.quote: Ten (10) to twelve (12) inches between the chest and the air bag module is recommended by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: It is illegal in Tennessee to allow any child under the age of 6 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck.
rules.quote: It is illegal in Tennessee to allow any child under the age of 6 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: It is against the law to allow a child between 6 and 12 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck on any state or interstate highway.
rules.quote: It is also against the law to allow any child between the ages of 6 and 12 to ride in the bed of a pickup truck on any state or interstate highway.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: The pickup-bed prohibition does not apply to an organized parade, procession or ceremonial event where the vehicle does not exceed twenty miles per hour, or to agricultural activities.
rules.quote: the vehicle must not exceed the speed of twenty (20) miles per hour. The other exception is when the child being transported in the bed of the vehicle is involved in agricultural activities.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: It is an offense to knowingly leave a child younger than 7 unattended in a motor vehicle on public property without supervision by a person at least 13 years of age, when conditions present a risk, the engine is running, or the keys are in the passenger compartment.
rules.quote: It is an offense for a person responsible for a child younger than 7 years of age to knowingly leave that child in a motor vehicle
extraQuotes: without being supervised in the motor vehicle by a person who is at least 13 years of age

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: Leaving a child unattended is a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a $200 fine for a first offense and $500 for a second or subsequent offense.
rules.quote: (b) A violation of this section is a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a fine of two hundred dollars ($200) for the first offense. (c) A second or subsequent violation of this section is a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a fine of five hundred dollars ($500).

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: A copy of a doctor's prescription must be carried in a vehicle using a medically prescribed modified child restraint device at all times.
rules.quote: A copy of a doctor's prescription should be carried in the vehicle utilizing the modified child restraint device (CRD) at all times.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: All occupants in 15-passenger vans must wear safety belts at all times; this is the law in Tennessee.
rules.quote: All occupants in 15-passenger vans must wear safety belts at all times. This is the law in Tennessee, as well as many other states.

rules.group: Safety belts, child restraints and occupant protection
rules.rule: No special endorsements or licenses are needed to operate a 15-passenger van in Tennessee.
rules.quote: There are no special endorsements or licenses needed to operate a 15-passenger van in the State of Tennessee.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Drivers must obey directions from law enforcement, highway construction personnel or school crossing guards even when those directions differ from what the lights and signs indicate.
rules.quote: Drivers must obey directions from these individuals, even if the directions are different than what the traffic lights and signs indicate.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The nine basic background colors are red, yellow, orange, black, brown, fluorescent yellow-green, green, white and blue.
rules.quote: The meanings of the nine basic background colors of sighs should be memorized.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Red is used only as a background color for STOP signs, ALL WAY/FOUR-WAY plates, DO-NOT-ENTER messages, WRONG WAY signs and on Interstate route markers.
rules.quote: RED is used only as a background color for STOP signs, multiple supplemental plates (FOUR-WAY or ALL WAY), DO-NOT-ENTER messages, WRONG WAY signs and on Interstate route markers.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Orange is used as a background color for construction and maintenance signs and shall not be used for any other purpose.
rules.quote: ORANGE is used as a background color for construction and maintenance signs and shall not be used for any other purpose.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Yellow is used as a background color for warning signs, except where orange is specified, and for school signs.
rules.quote: YELLOW is used as a background color for warning signs, except where orange is specified, and for school signs.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Brown is used as a background color for guide information signs related to points of recreational or cultural interest.
rules.quote: BROWN is used as a background color for guide information signs related to points of recreational cultural interest.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Green is used as a background color for guide signs, mileposts, and as a legend color with a white background for permissive parking regulations.
rules.quote: GREEN is used as a background color for guide signs (other than those using brown or white), mileposts and as a legend color with a white background for permissive parking regulations.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Blue is used as a background color for information signs related to motorist services, including police services and rest areas, and the Emergency Route Marker.
rules.quote: BLUE is used as a background color for information signs related to motorist services (including police services and rest areas) and the Emergency Route Marker.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Fluorescent yellow-green is the color for school zones and other pedestrian traffic areas such as crosswalks.
rules.quote: FLUORESCENT YELLOW-GREEN IS THE COLOR FOR SCHOOL ZONES!

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Fluorescent pink is used for incident management traffic control signage for incidents such as accidents, wildland fires, floods and hazardous material spills.
rules.quote: FLUORESCENT PINK (sometimes called "coral") is used for incident management traffic control signage when needed for incidents such as traffic accidents, wildland fires, floods, and hazardous material spills

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: At a stop sign you must bring your car to a complete stop, not going beyond the crosswalk, and if you cannot see, proceed cautiously to a point where you can see and go only if it is safe.
rules.quote: you must bring your car to a complete stop, not going beyond the crosswalk. IF you cannot see, then proceed cautiously to a point where you can see, and then go only if you can do so safely.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: An ALL WAY red rectangle added below a stop sign means all traffic approaching the intersection must stop.
rules.quote: ALL WAY: Red Rectangle –Added below a stop sign. It means all traffic approaching this intersection must stop.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A yield sign means you must slow down and enter the intersection with caution, and stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching.
rules.quote: This three-sided sign means that you are approaching an intersection and must stop and wait when other vehicles are approaching from the right or left on the other roadway. If you are sure no other cars are coming you need not come to a complete stop but you must slow down and enter the intersection with caution. Always stop when traffic is heavy.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The round railroad advance-warning sign means you are approaching a railroad grade crossing and must slow down and be ready to stop.
rules.quote: This circular sign always means that you are approaching a railroad grade crossing. You must slow down and be ready to stop.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The crossbuck is placed at all railroad grade crossings and shows exactly where the tracks are located, with smaller signs below showing the number of tracks.
rules.quote: This is known as a crossbuck sign. It is placed at all railroad grade crossings and shows exactly where the tracks are located.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Flashing lights on a crossbuck mean a train is coming; always stop and remain stopped until the train has passed.
rules.quote: Flashing lights on a crossbuck mean that a train is coming. Always stop when the lights are flashing. Remain stopped until the train has passed.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Stop when the lights begin flashing and before the gate comes down, and remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing.
rules.quote: Stop when the lights begin flashing and before the gate comes down. Remain stopped until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A diamond-shaped sign warns of a hazardous or unexpected condition ahead and calls for caution and usually a slower speed.
rules.quote: Diamond Shape — Hazardous Or Unexpected Condition Ahead These signs call for caution and usually for a slower speed.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A rectangular sign conveys special laws, regulations or important information, and some guide signs.
rules.quote: Rectangular Shape - Special Laws, Regulations or Important Information, Some Guide Signs

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A white background with a red circle and a diagonal line through it means "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.
rules.quote: Signs having a white background and a red circle and a line diagonally through them mean "NO" according to what is shown behind the red symbol.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: In Tennessee it is illegal to stand on a roadway to solicit a ride.
rules.quote: In Tennessee, it is illegal to stand on a roadway to solicit a ride.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The turn sign is used to mark turns with a recommended speed of 30 m.p.h. or less.
rules.quote: The turn sign is used to mark turns with a recommended speed of 30 m.p.h. or less.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The curve sign is used to mark curves with recommended speeds in the range between 30 and 55 m.p.h.
rules.quote: The curve sign is used to mark curves with recommended speeds in the range between 30 and 55 m.p.h.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The reverse turn sign marks two turns in opposite directions that are less than 600 feet apart.
rules.quote: The reverse turn sign is used to mark two turns in opposite directions that are less than 600 feet apart.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The falling-rocks sign warns of rocks that may be in the road, not of rocks that may strike from overhead.
rules.quote: This sign warns of rocks that may be in the road, not of rocks which may strike you from overhead. Watch the roadway, not the hill.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: In work areas a person with a sign or flag may control traffic and you must obey their directions.
rules.quote: In work areas, a person with a sign or flag may control traffic. You must obey the directions of these persons.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Flashing arrow panels alert approaching drivers of lane closures and you must begin to merge into the remaining open lanes well in advance of the sign.
rules.quote: Flashing arrow panels alert approaching drivers of lane closures. You must begin to merge into the remaining open lane(s) well in advance of this sign.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Barricades, vertical panels, concrete barriers, drums and cones guide drivers through work zones; keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and don't change lanes until completely clear of the work zone.
rules.quote: When driving near these devices, keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and obey the posted speed limit. As you leave the work zone, stay in your lane and maintain your speed. Don't change lanes until you are completely clear of the work zone.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: If an interstate guide sign is marked EXIT ONLY, all traffic in the lanes directly below the arrows must exit.
rules.quote: If an interstate guide sign is marked with the above sign, all traffic in the lane(s) directly below the arrows MUST exit.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Parking spaces displaying the blue handicap sign are reserved, and use of reserved handicapped spaces by others is prohibited by law.
rules.quote: The use of reserved handicapped spaces by others is prohibited by law.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Interstate reference markers are installed every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled urban sections and display route number, direction of travel and the log mile in tenths of a mile.
rules.quote: the state has installed interstate reference markers every 1,000 feet along heavily traveled sections.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Standard traffic lights are red, yellow and green, from top to bottom respectively.
rules.quote: Standard traffic lights are red, yellow and green, from top to bottom respectively.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Red means stop behind the crosswalk or stop line; unless otherwise posted you may turn right on red after a complete stop when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.
rules.quote: Stop behind crosswalk or stop line. Unless otherwise posted, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Yellow means prepare to stop, you must stop if it is safe to do so, and you must not speed up to beat the light.
rules.quote: You must stop if it is safe to do so. Do not speed up to beat the light.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Tennessee law only requires the yellow light to be exhibited for a minimum of three seconds before the red light.
rules.quote: Tennessee law only requires the yellow light to be exhibited for a minimum of three seconds before the red light.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Green means go if the intersection is clear, and you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection at light change.
rules.quote: Go IF the intersection is clear. You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection at light change.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, the same as a stop sign, then yield and proceed when safe.
rules.quote: FLASHING RED Complete stop. Same as stop sign. Look both ways, yield to traffic and pedestrians and proceed when it is safe to do so.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution at the intersection.
rules.quote: FLASHING YELLOW Slow down and proceed with caution at the intersection.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: On a green protected arrow you have the right-of-way and may drive only in the direction of the arrow after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.
rules.quote: When the arrow is green, you have the right-of-way and may drive the vehicle only in the direction of the arrow, after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited even if other lanes have a green signal.
rules.quote: When the arrow is red or your lane has the red light, all turns are prohibited. This is true even if other lanes of traffic have a green signal and your path through the intersection appears to be clear.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A flashing yellow arrow allows a left turn after yielding to all oncoming traffic and to bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk.
rules.quote: If you see a flashing yellow arrow,youareallowedtoturn left after yielding to all oncoming traffic and to any bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalk.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Tennessee state law requires that if a signal is not working the intersection is to be treated as if it were an all-way stop intersection.
rules.quote: Tennessee state law requires that if a signal is not working, the intersection is to be treated as if it were a ll-way stop intersection.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Tennessee law defines a pedestrian as any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair.
rules.quote: Tennessee law defines a pedestrian as any person afoot or using a motorized or non-motorized wheelchair.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: The WALK signal or walking person symbol indicates when it is safe to cross the street or intersection.
rules.quote: displays the word "WALK" or a symbol of a person walking when it is safe to cross the street or intersection.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A green arrow means you can drive in the lane beneath it, a red X means you cannot, a flashing yellow X means the lane is for turning only, and a steady yellow X means the lane use is changing and you should move out of it.
rules.quote: A green arrow means you can drive in the lane beneath it. • A red "X" means you CANNOT drive in the lane below. • A flashing yellow "X" means the lane is only for turning. • A steady yellow "X" means that the use/direction of the lane is changing and you should move out of it as soon as it is safe to do so.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: A solid white line indicates the right edge of the traffic lane and a solid or broken yellow line indicates the left edge of traffic lanes going in your direction.
rules.quote: A solid white line indicates the right edge of the traffic lane on a road. A solid or broken yellow line indicates the left edge of traffic lanes going in your direction.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: If you find yourself with yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.
rules.quote: If you ever find yourself with yellow to your right and white to your left, you are going the wrong way.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Broken yellow lines mean you may cross the line to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.
rules.quote: Broken yellow lines mean that you MAY cross the line to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Two solid yellow lines between lanes mean you may not cross from either direction, though you may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road if safe.
rules.quote: Two solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic mean you MAY NOT cross the lines from either direction, even if no oncoming traffic is in view. You may cross a solid yellow line to turn into a driveway or side road if it is safe to do so.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Where there is both a solid and a broken yellow line, you may not pass if the solid yellow line is on your side; if the broken line is on your side you are in the passing zone.
rules.quote: you may not pass if the solid yellow line is on your side. If the broken yellow line is on your side, you are in the "passing zone" and may pass if it is safe to do so. You must safely return to your side of the roadway before the passing zone ends.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Broken white lines between lanes mean you may cross to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.
rules.quote: Broken white lines between lanes of traffic mean you may cross the lines to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: One solid white line between lanes means you should stay in your lane and not cross to pass, and you should not cross a double solid white line.
rules.quote: One solid white line between lanes of traffic means that you should stay in your lane and should not cross the line to pass (unless an emergency situation requires you to change lanes). Also, you should not cross a double solid white line.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Not all crosswalks are marked, and you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are in or about to enter the crosswalk or street.
rules.quote: However, not all crosswalks are marked. You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are in or are about to enter the crosswalk or street.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: If a stop line is painted, the vehicle must stop behind it; if not, stop before crossing the first line of a marked crosswalk, or before the front bumper crosses the white edge line of the cross street.
rules.quote: (B) Stop the vehicle before crossing the first line of the crosswalk (if the crosswalk is marked), and (C) Stop the vehicle before the front bumper crosses the white edge line of the cross street

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: HOV lanes are designated by a diamond-shaped marking in the center of the lane, and road signs indicate the minimum number of passengers required and the times restrictions apply.
rules.quote: High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lanes are designated on highways by a diamond-shaped marking in the center of the lane.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: If you are traveling in a lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY, you must turn in the direction of the arrow.
rules.quote: If you are traveling in a lane marked with a curved arrow and the word ONLY, you must turn in the direction of the arrow.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: If your lane is marked with both a curved and a straight arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow or go straight.
rules.quote: If your lane is marked with both a curved and a straight arrow, you may turn in the direction of the arrow or you may go straight.

rules.group: Traffic signs, signals and pavement markings
rules.rule: Red reflectors facing you always mean you are facing traffic the wrong way and could have a head-on collision.
rules.quote: Red reflectors always mean you are facing traffic the wrong way and could have a head-on collision.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: You must obey traffic officers at all times, even when instructed to do something that would ordinarily be a violation.
rules.quote: You must obey traffic officers at all times. There will be times when an officer will instruct you to do something that ordinarily would be a violation of traffic regulations.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: While traveling on a downgrade you must never coast with the transmission in neutral, and manual-transmission drivers must not coast with the clutch depressed.
rules.quote: While traveling on a downgrade, NEVER coast with the transmission of the vehicle in neutral. Also, drivers of manual transmission vehicles must not coast with the clutch depressed.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Coasting with the gears in neutral is illegal.
rules.quote: Don't coast with the gears in neutral (it's illegal) or with the clutch pedal pushed down except when shifting gears.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Headlights must be turned on 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
rules.quote: Your car headlights must be turned on 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Headlights must be on at any time when daylight is not good enough to see persons or vehicles clearly at a distance of 200 feet ahead.
rules.quote: At any time when daylight is not good enough for you to see persons or vehicles clearly at a distance of 200 feet ahead

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Headlights must be on when rain, mist, snow or other precipitation requires constant use of windshield wipers — it is Tennessee law.
rules.quote: using headlights when wipers are in use is not just a good safety precaution — it's Tennessee law!
extraQuotes: When rain, mist, snow, or other precipitation requires constant use of windshield wipers.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: You must dim high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet or when following another vehicle within 500 feet.
rules.quote: you must dim or lower the beam when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet (approximately the distance of one city block) or when you are following another vehicle within 500 feet.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: The law requires a vehicle stopped or parked on a road or shoulder to have parking lights on when limited visibility conditions exist, and driving on parking lights alone in limited visibility is against the law.
rules.quote: The law requires a vehicle stopped or parked on a road or shoulder to have parking lights on when limited visibility conditions exist.
extraQuotes: When there is limited visibility, the use of parking lights alone is not only unsafe, it is against the law.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: It is illegal to have auxiliary lights or fog lights on by themselves or on at times when you are required to dim high beam headlights.
rules.quote: It is also illegal to have auxiliary lights or fog lights on by themselves or on at times when you are required to dim high beam headlights.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Effective January 1, 2018, no vehicle in Tennessee may be equipped with steady-burning lights displaying to the front in any color other than white or amber, with exceptions for certain vehicles.
rules.quote: Effective January 1, 2018, no vehicle operated in Tennessee shall be equipped with any steady-burning lights that display to the front of the vehicle in any color other than white or amber or in any combination of colors other than white and amber.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Effective January 1, 2018, no vehicle in Tennessee may be equipped with flashing lights displaying to the front other than factory installed emergency flashers.
rules.quote: no vehicle operated in Tennessee shall be equipped with any flashing lights in any color or combination of colors that display to the front of the vehicle, other than factory installed emergency flashers.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: It is against the law for an unauthorized private vehicle to have a blue flashing emergency light, or a combination of blue and red flashing lights, installed, maintained or visibly shown.
rules.quote: It is against the law for an unauthorized private vehicle to have a blue flashing emergency light or combination of blue and red flashing emergency lights installed, maintained or visibly shown on the vehicle in any manner.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: The law requires headlights that will enable you to see clearly any person on the highway at least two hundred feet ahead of your car.
rules.quote: The law requires headlights that will enable you to see clearly any person on the highway at least two hundred (200) feet ahead of your car.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: When driving through dense fog, heavy rain or snow during the daytime you must turn on your low beam headlights — a requirement of Tennessee law.
rules.quote: WHEN DRIVING THROUGH DENSE FOG, HEAVY RAIN OR SNOW DURING THE DAYTIME, TURN ON YOU LOW BEAM HEADLIGHTS
extraQuotes: it is also a requirement of Tennessee law.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: In fog or mist never put your headlights on high beam because the light will be reflected back into your eyes.
rules.quote: In fog or mist, never put your headlights on high beam because the light will be reflected back into your eyes.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Tennessee law requires any motor vehicle transporting litter or material likely to fall or blow onto the highway to be in an enclosed space or fully covered by a tarpaulin.
rules.quote: Tennessee law requires any motor vehicle transporting litter or any material, likely to fall or be blown off onto the highway, to be in an enclosed space or fully covered by a tarpaulin.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Littering fines start at $50 and can be up to $3,000 based on the amount of litter, plus up to 40 hours of public service removing litter and, at the court's discretion, up to 8 additional hours at a waste recycling center.
rules.quote: Fines start at $50 and can be up to $3,000 based upon the amount of litter. A person convicted of littering is required to spend up to 40 hours of public service removing litter and at the discretion of the court, spend up to 8 additional hours of working in awaste recycling center.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: It is against the law to drive slower than the posted minimum speed under normal driving conditions, and it is against the law to drive so slowly that you block traffic even where no minimum is posted.
rules.quote: If there is noposted minimum speed, it is still against the law to drive so slowly that you block traffic.
extraQuotes: It is against the law to drive slower than the postedminimum speed under normal driving conditions

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: You are considered to be driving a slow-moving vehicle if you are traveling 10 miles per hour or more below the lawful maximum speed.
rules.quote: You are considered to be driving a slow-moving vehicle if you are traveling at a rate of speed that is 10 miles per hour or more below the lawful maximum speed.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely.
rules.quote: If five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway may not attempt to pass it, and no driver may drive between vehicles in a properly identified funeral procession except when directed by a traffic officer.
rules.quote: Vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway may not attempt to pass such procession; and • No operator of a vehicle shall drive between vehicles in a properly identified funeral procession except when directed to do so by a traffic officer.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: The Basic Speed Rule is not a Tennessee law but a general safety principle that the speed you may drive is limited by current conditions.
rules.quote: The Basic Speed Rule (BSR) is not a Tennessee law, but it is a general safety principle.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 m.p.h.
rules.quote: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 m.p.h.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: The maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways is 70 m.p.h.
rules.quote: The maximum speed set by Tennessee law for interstate highways is 70 m.p.h.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: In the more congested urban or metropolitan areas of Tennessee interstates the limit is typically 55 m.p.h.
rules.quote: In the more congested urban or metropolitan areas of Tennessee interstates, the limit is typically 55 m.p.h.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: It is unlawful to drive a vehicle less than 55 m.p.h. in the left-most lane of any interstate highway unless traffic congestion and flow prevent safe driving at that speed.
rules.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle less than 55 m.p.h. in the left most lane of any Interstate highway, unless traffic congestion and flow prevent safe driving at such speed.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: On the interstates the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) is 45 m.p.h.
rules.quote: On the interstates, the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) is 45 m.p.h., and under normal driving conditions, all vehicles must travel at least this fast

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Exceeding the school zone speed limit is by law considered to be reckless driving, with an automatic six points added to your driving record.
rules.quote: Exceeding the school zone speed limit is by law considered to be reckless driving. The penalty includes an automatic six points added to your driving record

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Tennessee law mandates a minimum fine of $250 and up to a maximum fine of $500 for violations of the speed limit posted in active work zones.
rules.quote: TENNESSEE LAW MANDATES A MINIMUM FINE OF $250 DOLLARS AND UP TO A MAXIMUM FINE OF $500 DOLLARS FOR VIOLATIONS OF THE SPEED LIMIT POSTED IN ACTIVE WORK ZONES.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: Under Tennessee law, speed violations in work zones where the speed has been reduced and workers are present result in a fine up to a maximum of $500.
rules.quote: Under Tennessee law, speed violations that occur in the work zones where the speed has been reduced and where employees of the Department of Transportation as well as other construction workers are present, will result in a fine up to a maximum of $500 dollars.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: If there are no reduced speed limit postings in a work zone, drivers should obey the normal posted speed limit.
rules.quote: if there are no reduced speed limit postings, drivers should obey the normal posted speed limit.

rules.group: Rules of the road — basic rules, lights, speed
rules.rule: You can be ticketed and be the cause of an accident for being a last chance merger in a work zone.
rules.quote: Merge early! You can be ticketed and be the cause of an accident for being a last chance merger.

rules.rule: Tennessee law states that a driver shall not follow another vehicle more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for speed, traffic and highway condition.
rules.quote: Tennessee law states: "The driver of a motor vehicle shall not follow another vehicle more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway."

rules.rule: During inclement weather, interstate driving at higher speeds and night driving, the two-second rule should be increased to a minimum of four seconds, including when following a motorcycle.
rules.quote: A minimum of four seconds should allow for better reaction time and a safer space cushion under these conditions including following a motorcycle.

rules.topic: Two-second rule applies at any speed
rules.rule: The two-second principle holds true at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits.
rules.quote: This principle will hold true at any speed on state and U.S. highways with moderate speed limits.

rules.rule: With ABS, apply firm steady pressure to the brake pedal and never pump the pedal.
rules.quote: When slowing or stopping, apply firm, steady pressure to the brake pedal. Never pump the pedal with ABS.

rules.rule: The three steps in stopping a vehicle are perception time, reaction time and braking time.
rules.quote: There are three steps in stopping a vehicle: • Perception time

rules.rule: Average reaction time — from perception of danger to the start of braking — is 2/3 of a second (about .66 second), with perception about .50 second.
rules.quote: The average is 2/3 of a second
extraQuotes: Perception About .50 second
Reaction About .66 second

rules.rule: Every driver approaching a stop sign shall stop before entering the nearest side of a crosswalk or at a clearly marked stop line; if neither is present, stop at a point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic, and stop before entering the intersection.
rules.quote: Tennessee law states: Every driver approaching a stop sign shall stop before entering the nearest side of a crosswalk, or stop at a clearly marked stop line. If neither is present, then (1) stop at a point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway, and (2) stop before entering the actual intersection.

rules.rule: Tennessee Code defines "stop" as "complete cessation of movement."
rules.quote: Tennessee Code defines "stop" as "complete cessation of movement."

rules.rule: If no pavement markings are present, stop when the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign's placement on the roadside.
rules.quote: If no pavement markings are present, stop when the front of your vehicle is even with the stop sign's placement on the roadside.

rules.rule: Rolling stops are dangerous and illegal, and are grounds for a traffic ticket and for failing the driver examination road test.
rules.quote: Rolling stops are grounds for receiving a traffic ticket AND for failing the driver examination road test.
extraQuotes: Rolling stops are dangerous and illegal

rules.rule: A complete stop is required at a flashing red traffic light, just as with a stop sign.
rules.quote: A complete stop is required at a flashing red traffic light, just as with a stop sign.

rules.rule: You must stop completely when directed to stop by a flag person at a road construction site or by a police officer.
rules.quote: You must stop completely when directed to stop by a flag person at a road construction site or by a police officer directing you to stop in any situation.

rules.rule: Every motor vehicle should be driven at a rate of speed that will permit the vehicle to be stopped before reaching the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
rules.quote: Every motor vehicle should be driven at a rate of speed that will permit the vehicle to be stopped before reaching the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

rules.rule: When you approach a railroad crossing and a train is coming, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks and never stop on the tracks.
rules.quote: you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks. Never stop on the railroad crossing tracks.

rules.rule: Crossings equipped with electric or mechanical signal devices require the operator to stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet, from the nearest rail.
rules.quote: Railroad crossings equipped with electric or mechanical signal devices require the operator to bring the vehicle to a complete stop within 50 feet, and no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and shall not proceed until it is safe.

rules.rule: Trains are required to signal a horn when they are approximately 1,500 feet from passing through a railroad crossing.
rules.quote: Trains are required to signal a horn when they are approximately 1,500 feet from passing through a railroad crossing.

rules.topic: Vehicles required to stop at crossings
rules.rule: Church or school buses, common carriers such as taxis and other vehicles transporting passengers for hire, and vehicles transporting flammables, explosives or other dangerous articles must stop before crossing any railroad grade crossing.
rules.quote: Church or school buses, regardless of whether such buses are carrying any passengers at the time of crossing; • Common carriers, such as taxis or other vehicles transporting passengers for hire; • Vehicles transporting flammables, explosives or other dangerous articles as cargo or part of a cargo.

rules.rule: Violations of railroad signals or signs carry the same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices.
rules.quote: Violations of railroad signals or signs carry the same penalties as violations of other traffic control devices.

rules.rule: It is against the law to drive through lowered gates, and you must not cross until the gates are fully raised and the lights have stopped flashing.
rules.quote: Never drive around a crossing gate that has extended down. If the gates are down, stop and stay in place. It's against the law to drive through lowered gates.

rules.rule: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, all occupants should exit immediately and get away from the tracks even if no train is visible, then call the number on the Emergency Notification System sign or 911.
rules.quote: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, all occupants should exit the vehicle immediately and get away from the tracks even if you do not see a train. Locate the Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign and call the emergency number provided

rules.rule: If a train is approaching a stalled vehicle, run toward the train at a 45 degree angle to be away from and behind the point of impact.
rules.quote: If a train is approaching, run toward the train at a 45 degree angle. This allows you to be away from and behind the point of impact, to prevent injury.

rules.rule: If you approach a railroad crossing at which a stop sign is posted you must come to a complete stop and proceed only after looking both ways.
rules.quote: If you approach a railroad crossing at which a stop sign is posted, you must come to a complete stop and proceed across the tracks only after looking both ways to make sure a train is not approaching.

rules.rule: A driver meeting a school bus or church bus with red stop warning signal lights flashing must reduce speed and come to a complete stop while the stop signal arm is extended, and remain stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus resumes motion.
rules.quote: Any driver meeting a school bus or church bus on which the red stop warning signal lights are flashing should reduce his speed and bring the vehicle to a complete stop while the bus stop signal arm is extended. The vehicle must remain stopped until the stop arm is pulled back and the bus resumes motion.

rules.rule: A driver approaching a school or church bus from the rear shall not pass when red stop warning lights are flashing and must come to a complete stop.
rules.quote: Any driver approaching a school bus or church bus from the rear shall not pass the bus when red stop warning signal lights are flashing. The vehicle must come to a complete stop when the bus is stopped.

rules.rule: Never pass on the right side of a stopped school bus, as this is where the children enter or exit; it is illegal.
rules.quote: Never pass on the right side of the bus, as this is where the children enter or exit. This is illegal and can have tragic results.

rules.rule: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load and unload children, drivers from ALL directions are required to stop until the bus resumes motion.
rules.quote: When a school bus is stopped at an intersection to load and unload children, drivers from ALL directions are required to stop until the bus resumes motion

rules.rule: Failing to stop for a stopped school bus is a Class A misdemeanor and the driver can be fined between $250 and $1,000.
rules.quote: It is a Class A misdemeanor and the driver can be fined between $250 and $1,000 for not stopping for a stopped school bus.

rules.rule: On a highway with separate roadways divided by a median or barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic, the driver need not stop for a school bus but should proceed with caution.
rules.quote: When driving on a highway with separate roadways for traffic in opposite directions, divided by median space or a barrier not suitable for vehicular traffic, the driver need not stop, but should proceed with caution.

rules.topic: Turn lane is not a barrier
rules.rule: A turn lane in the middle of a four-lane highway is not a barrier, so drivers meeting a stopped school bus on that road must stop in both directions.
rules.quote: A turn lane in the middle of a four-lane highway is NOT considered a barrier, but a fifth lane that is suitable for vehicular traffic. Drivers meeting a stopped school bus on this type of road would be required to stop in both directions.

rules.rule: Flashing yellow lights on the front and back of a school bus mean the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children and motorists should slow down and prepare to stop.
rules.quote: When the yellow lights on the front and back of the bus are flashing the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children. Motorists should slow down and prepare to stop their vehicles.
