rules.rule: Flashing red lights with the stop arm extended indicate the bus has stopped and children are getting on or off, and motorists must stop and wait until the lights are off, the arm withdrawn and the bus begins moving.
rules.quote: Motorists must stop their cars and wait until the red flashing lights are turned off, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving before they start driving again.

rules.rule: Children should stay ten feet away from the school bus and never go behind the bus.
rules.quote: Children should stay ten feet away from the school bus and NEVER go behind the bus.

rules.rule: When stopped by police, drive as closely as is safely practical to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, stop and park, keep hands on the wheel and remain in the vehicle unless asked to get out.
rules.quote: Drive as closely as is safely practical to the right-hand edge or curb of the road, clear of any intersection, stop and park.
extraQuotes: Keep all vehicle doors closed and remain in the vehicle unless asked to get out.

rules.rule: Drivers should advise officers if they have a handgun permit and if they are armed.
rules.quote: Drivers should advise officers if they have a handgun permit and if they are armed.

rules.rule: If directed to pull over by someone in an unmarked police car, you may drive slowly a short distance to the nearest area where there are other people.
rules.quote: If you find yourself being directed to pull over and stop by someone in an UNMARKED police car, you may drive slowly a short distance to the nearest area where there are other people

rules.rule: The law does not give anyone the right-of-way; it only says who must yield it.
rules.quote: The law does not really give anyone the right-of-way. It only says who must yield the right-of-way.

rules.rule: Look first to the left to make sure cross traffic is yielding, then look right, and if stopped look both left and right just before you start moving.
rules.quote: The Left-Right-Left Rule: Look first to the left to make sure cross traffic is yielding the right-of-way. Then look for traffic from the right. If stopped, look both left and right just before you start moving.

rules.rule: It is always illegal to block an intersection, whether it is marked or not.
rules.quote: It is always illegal to block an intersection, whether it is marked or not.

rules.rule: You must yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk, or when the pedestrian is on your half of the roadway or approaching so closely from the other half as to be in danger.
rules.quote: When pedestrians are in a crosswalk (marked or unmarked) or when the pedestrian is upon the half of the roadway upon which your vehicle is traveling or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the roadway as to be in danger

rules.rule: In a marked school zone when a warning flasher is in operation, the driver shall stop to yield to a pedestrian crossing within a marked or unmarked crosswalk and remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway on which the vehicle is stopped.
rules.quote: the driver of a vehicle shall stop to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing the roadway within a marked or unmarked crosswalk. The driver shall remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway on which the vehicle is stopped.

rules.rule: You must yield when your vehicle crosses a sidewalk while entering or exiting a driveway, alley or parking lot, and it is illegal to drive on a sidewalk except to cross it.
rules.quote: When your vehicle crosses a sidewalk while entering or exiting a driveway, alley or parking lot. It is illegal to drive on a sidewalk except to cross it

rules.rule: You must yield to a blind or visually impaired pedestrian using a guide dog or a white cane (or white with red tip), or a hearing-impaired person with a dog on a blaze orange leash, stopping at least 10 feet away until the person is off the roadway, and you must not use your horn.
rules.quote: Stop at least 10 feet away until the person is off the roadway. Do not use your horn, as it could startle the blind pedestrian

rules.rule: When starting from a parked position, wait for all moving traffic to pass.
rules.quote: When starting from a parked position, wait for all moving traffic to pass.

rules.rule: When turning left you must wait for oncoming traffic going straight ahead or turning right.
rules.quote: When turning left, you must wait for oncoming traffic going straight ahead or turning right.

rules.rule: When entering a main road from a driveway, alley, parking lot or roadside you must yield to all vehicles already on the main road.
rules.quote: When entering a main road from a driveway, alley, parking lot or roadside, you must yield to all vehicles already on the main road.

rules.rule: When entering a roundabout, traffic circle or rotary you must yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
rules.quote: When entering a roundabout, traffic circle or rotary (also known as "town squares"), you must yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

rules.rule: When approaching a fire station you should yield to any emergency vehicle that is about to back into, or is backing into, the driveway entrance.
rules.quote: When approaching a fire station, you should yield to any emergency vehicle that is about to back into, or is already in the process of backing into, the driveway entrance to the station.

rules.rule: You must yield to any vehicles already in the intersection, even if you have the green traffic light.
rules.quote: To any vehicles already in the intersection, even if you have the green traffic light

rules.rule: At "T" intersections the vehicles on the road that is ending must yield to oncoming traffic from both directions on the main road.
rules.quote: At "T" intersections where one road dead-ends into another main crossing roadway, the vehicles on the road ending must yield to oncoming traffic from both directions on the main road

rules.rule: At intersections marked as ALL-WAY stops the vehicle reaching the intersection first gets to go first, and if more than one vehicle arrives at the same time yield to the vehicle on the right.
rules.quote: At intersections marked as ALL-WAY stops, the vehicle reaching the intersection first gets to go first (of course, ALL vehicles must stop). If more than one vehicle arrives at the same time, yield the right of way to the vehicle on the right

rules.rule: Where roads cross and there are no stop signs or signals, yield to any vehicle coming at the same time on your right.
rules.quote: Where roads cross and there are no stop signs or signals, yield to any vehicle coming at the same time on your right

rules.rule: You must yield the right-of-way to a police vehicle, fire engine, ambulance or other emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn, or a red or blue flashing light.
rules.quote: You must yield the right-of-way to a police vehicle, fire engine, ambulance or other emergency vehicle using a siren, air horn or a red or blue flashing light.

rules.topic: Pull to the right and stop
rules.rule: When an emergency vehicle approaches, all traffic meeting or being overtaken must yield and immediately drive to a position parallel to and as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb and stop, remaining stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed or an officer directs otherwise.
rules.quote: all traffic meeting or being overtaken must yield the right-of-way and immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to the right hand edge or curb of the roadway stop. You must remain in that stopped position until the emergency vehicle has passed or until you are directed to move by a police officer.

rules.rule: It is against the law to follow a fire truck or other emergency vehicle responding to an alarm, and illegal to take your vehicle within the block where the emergency vehicle has stopped.
rules.quote: It is against the law to follow a fire truck or other emergency vehicle responding to a fire alarm or other emergency. It is also illegal to take your vehicle within the block of where the emergency vehicle has stopped

rules.rule: Do not drive over any unprotected fire department hose unless the fire department official in command says it is okay.
rules.quote: do not drive over any unprotected fire department hose unless the fire department official in command says it is okay.

rules.rule: If the traffic light is red when an emergency vehicle approaches, stay where you are, and do not proceed on green until the emergency vehicle has passed or turned.
rules.quote: If the traffic light is red, stay where you are. If the light turns green before the emergency vehicle has passed, do NOT proceed on green.

rules.rule: You must yield the right-of-way to any transit vehicle that has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway from a bus stop.
rules.quote: You must yield the right-of-way to any transit vehicle (metro bus) that has signaled and is pulling back onto the roadway from a bus stop.

rules.rule: Tennessee's Move Over Law requires that when approaching any stationary emergency vehicle with lights flashing you must change into a lane not adjacent to that vehicle, or reduce speed and proceed with caution, on multi-lane roadways with two or more lanes moving in the same direction.
rules.quote: Tennessee's Move Over Law requires that when approaching any stationary emergency vehicle with lights flashing, you must make a lane change into a lane not adjacent to that of the vehicle, or proceed with caution by reducing the speed of the vehicle and maintaining a safe speed for the current road conditions.

rules.rule: The Move Over Law applies to interstates and any multi-lane highway with four or more lanes that has at least two lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction.
rules.quote: Tennessee law requires that motorists yield the lane closest to any emergency, maintenance or recovery vehicle that is stopped on the shoulder of the roadway. This applies to interstates and any multi-lane highway (with four or more lanes) that has at least two lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction.

rules.rule: The requirement to move over applies regardless of whether the emergency vehicle is on the right or left-hand side of the road.
rules.quote: This requirement to move over applies, regardless of whether the emergency vehicle is on the right or left-hand side of the road.

rules.rule: The Move Over Law covers police/highway patrol, ambulance or fire vehicles, utility vehicles, tow trucks or TDOT HELP vehicles, and TDOT maintenance vehicles or private road-work contractors.
rules.quote: Police or Highway Patrol vehicles; • Ambulance or Fire Fighting vehicles; • Utility vehicles that provide your electric, phone, natural gas and water services as well as solid waste "sanitation" vehicles; • Tow Trucks or TDOT HELP vehicles; • TDOT maintenance vehicles or private contractors involved in road construction or repair work.

rules.rule: The Move Over Law now also applies to all stationary motor vehicles, such as a car or truck, with their emergency flasher lights on.
rules.quote: this law now applies to all stationary motor vehicles, such as your car or truck, with their emergency flasher lights on.

rules.rule: Only when traffic conditions make a lane change unsafe may the motorist slow down and remain in the same lane.
rules.quote: ONLY when traffic conditions make it unsafe to make such lane change is the motorist allowed to respond to this situation by simply slowing down and remaining in the same lane.

rules.rule: Drivers must always yield the right of way to trains because it's the law.
rules.quote: Drivers must ALWAYS yield the right of way to trains because IT'S THE LAW.

rules.rule: Generally, pedestrians have the right-of-way at all intersections, and there is a crosswalk at every intersection even if not marked.
rules.quote: Generally, pedestrians have the right-of-way at all intersections. There is a crosswalk at every intersection, even if painted lines and boundaries do not mark the crossing.

rules.rule: Pedestrians must not suddenly leave a curb or other safe waiting place and walk into the path of traffic that is so close it is an immediate hazard.
rules.quote: pedestrians must not suddenly leave a curb or other safe waiting place and walk into the path of vehicle traffic if it so close that it is an immediate hazard.

rules.rule: Pedestrians must walk along sidewalks when available; it is unlawful for pedestrians to walk in the road where there are sidewalks.
rules.quote: Pedestrians must walk along sidewalks when available. It is unlawful for pedestrians to walk in the road where there are sidewalks.

rules.rule: When there are no sidewalks, always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic, and two or more pedestrians should walk in single file.
rules.quote: Two or more pedestrians should walk in single file and never side by side of each other.
extraQuotes: When there are no sidewalks, always walk on the left side of the road facing traffic

rules.rule: Pedestrians may not cross on a red or yellow traffic light unless facing a WALK signal, and if the DON'T WALK signal starts flashing while you are in the street, continue walking.
rules.quote: Pedestrians may NOT cross on a red or yellow traffic light, or on a red-green combines light unless facing a WALK signal.

rules.rule: Turn from the closest lane in the direction you are traveling to the closest legal lane in the direction you want to go.
rules.quote: The first rule of turning is to turn from the closest lane in the direction you are traveling to the closest legal lane in the direction you want to go.

rules.rule: You must turn on your turn signal lights at least 50 feet before the turn.
rules.quote: At least 50 feet before the turn, you must turn on your turn signal lights.

rules.rule: Use your turn signal at least 50 feet before the turn or lane change.
rules.quote: Use your turn signal at least 50 feet before the turn or lane change.

rules.rule: Give a signal for a right turn for at least 50 feet.
rules.quote: Give a signal for a right turn for at least 50 feet.

rules.rule: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not signal until you are in the intersection.
rules.quote: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not signal until you are in the intersection.

rules.rule: You should not use your signals to tell a driver behind you to pass, or to relay the turn intentions of vehicles ahead.
rules.quote: To signal a driver behind you to come around to pass your vehicle. • To relay the turn intentions of vehicles ahead of you to those drivers behind your vehicle.

rules.rule: Hand and arm signals may be used instead of turn signal lights, and the arm should be brought in during the actual turn to keep control of the steering wheel.
rules.quote: When you use hand signals, bring your arm in during the actual turn to keep control of the steering wheel.
extraQuotes: You may use either your vehicle turn signal lights or hand and arm signals.

rules.rule: Don't turn your wheels in the direction of the turn while waiting for oncoming traffic to pass, because a rear impact can push you into oncoming traffic.
rules.quote: Don't turn your wheels in the direction of the turn while waiting for oncoming traffic to pass. If you are hit from the rear while your wheels are turned, the impact can push you into oncoming traffic.

rules.topic: Left turn from two-way to two-way
rules.rule: Approach with the left side of the vehicle as close to the center line as possible and turn into the first lane past the center line, never turning wide into the right lane.
rules.quote: approach the turn with the left side of the vehicle as close to the center line as possible.
extraQuotes: be sure to turn into the first lane past the center line
Never turn "wide" into the right lane.

rules.rule: If the intersection has a lane signed or marked for left turns, you must not make the turn from any other lane.
rules.quote: If the intersection has a lane signed or marked for making left turns, do not make this turn from any other lane.

rules.rule: Center lines on two-way streets are yellow; center lines on one-way streets are white.
rules.quote: Center lines on two-way streets are yellow. • Center lines on one-way streets are white.

rules.rule: When turning left onto a one-way street, turn sharply into the first lane closest to the left curb.
rules.quote: You should turn into the first lane closest to the left curb.
extraQuotes: Turn sharply into the FIRST lane

rules.rule: When turning left from a one-way onto a one-way, approach in the traffic lane furthest to the left curb and turn sharply into the first lane on the left side.
rules.quote: Make your approach in the traffic lane furthermost to the left curb of the street. • Turn sharply into the first lane on the left side of the one-way street. DO NOT TURN WIDE.

rules.rule: A left turn on red is permitted at intersections not marked "No Turns on Red" when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street, after coming to a complete stop.
rules.quote: you may make a left turn on red when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. You must come to a complete stop at the light prior to making the turn, the same as right turns on red.

rules.topic: One-way to two-way, no left on red
rules.rule: You cannot make a left turn on a red light when turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street.
rules.quote: You CANNOT make this left turn on a red light.

rules.rule: Get as close as is practical to the right curb or road edge without interfering with pedestrians, bicyclists or parked vehicles, and move into the travel lane closest to the right curb.
rules.quote: Get as close as is practical to the right curb or road edge without interfering with pedestrians, bicyclists or parked vehicles.

rules.rule: Do not pass a truck on the right if there is a possibility it might make a right turn, because large trucks and buses must make wide turns.
rules.quote: Large trucks and buses MUST make wide turns. Sometimes they must leave an open space to the right just before the turn. To avoid an accident, do not pass a truck on the right if there is a possibility that it might make a right turn.

rules.rule: A vehicle in the second lane can make the same turn as a vehicle in the first lane only when a lane use control sign or marking permits it.
rules.quote: A vehicle in the second lane can make the same turn as a vehicle in the first lane only when a lane use control sign or marking permits it.

rules.rule: Always travel around a roundabout to the right, in a counter-clockwise direction.
rules.quote: Always travel around a roundabout to the right, in a counter-clockwise direction.

rules.rule: Upon reaching the roundabout, yield to vehicles already within the circulating traffic and enter when there is a gap; once inside do not stop unless directed by signs, signals or a traffic officer.
rules.quote: Enter the roundabout when there is a gap in traffic and once inside do not stop unless directed to do so by signs, signals or a traffic officer.
extraQuotes: Upon reaching the roundabout, yield to vehicles already within the circulating traffic

rules.rule: Within the roundabout, proceed at a slower speed, usually posted at 15 to 25 m.p.h.
rules.quote: Within the roundabout, proceed at a slower speed (usually posted at 15 to 25 m.p.h.).

rules.rule: In a multi-lane roundabout, do not overtake or pass any vehicles.
rules.quote: In a multi-lane roundabout, do not overtake or pass any vehicles.

rules.rule: Always indicate your exit from a roundabout using your right turn signal and watch for pedestrians in or approaching the crosswalk on the street you are exiting.
rules.quote: Always indicate your exit using your right turn signal. Watch for pedestrians in or approaching the crosswalk on the street you are exiting and yield the right-of-way if necessary.

rules.rule: You may not make a U-turn at any intersection where a traffic light or police officer is controlling traffic, where you cannot see traffic from both directions for at least 500 feet, where prohibited by signs or markings, or between intersections in a city.
rules.quote: At any rural or urban location where you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for at least 500 feet in each direction.

rules.rule: It is illegal in Tennessee for any driver to make a U-turn on an interstate highway, and emergency crossovers are for emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.
rules.quote: It is illegal in Tennessee for any driver to make a U-turn on an interstate highway. Emergency crossovers are for the use of emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews only.

rules.rule: When driving on a road without center line markings where vehicles come from each direction, drivers must give others going in the opposite direction at least half the road.
rules.quote: drivers must give others going in the opposite direction at least half the road.

rules.rule: The center lane of a two-way, three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for turning left.
rules.quote: The center lane of a two-way, three-lane or five-lane highway is used only for turning left.

rules.rule: You may drive left of center only when passing a vehicle going the same direction, passing an obstruction, on a one-way road, or when turning left.
rules.quote: Drive on the right of the road except when: • Passing another vehicle going in the same direction as your vehicle; • Driving to the left of center to pass an obstruction in the road
extraQuotes: A road is marked for one way traffic; • You are turning left.

rules.rule: Do not drive within, across or over any median strip or barrier separating the roadways of a divided highway, except at an authorized crossover or intersection or when officially directed.
rules.quote: Do not drive within, across or over any median strip or barrier separating these roadways. It is only allowed at an authorized crossover or intersection, or when you are officially directed to do so.

rules.rule: Crossovers are permitted only at paved openings provided on four-lane highways, and there are no crossovers provided for traffic on interstates.
rules.quote: such a crossover is PERMITTED ONLY at paved openings provided on four-lane highways. There are NO crossovers provided for traffic on interstates.

rules.rule: Shared center turn lanes cannot be used for passing and cannot be used for travel farther than 300 feet.
rules.quote: These lanes cannot be used for passing and cannot be used for travel farther than 300 feet.

rules.rule: When vehicles enter the shared center turn lane from opposite directions, the first vehicle to enter the lane has the right-of-way.
rules.quote: When vehicles enter the turn lane from opposite directions, the first vehicle to enter the lane has the right-of-way.

rules.rule: Do not travel in the center turn lane to access a left turn lane at an intersection.
rules.quote: Do NOT travel in the center turn lane to access a left turn lane at an intersection.

rules.rule: Reversible lanes carry traffic in one direction at certain times and the opposite direction at other times, and are usually marked by double-broken yellow lines.
rules.quote: These lanes are called "reversible lanes" and are usually marked by double-broken yellow lines.

rules.rule: Do not travel in a reserved lane unless operating the type of vehicle indicated, or unless you must turn across the reserved lane in the next half block distance.
rules.quote: Do NOT travel in one of these lanes unless operating the type of vehicle indicated, or unless you must turn across the reserved lane in the next half block distance.

rules.rule: "HOV 2" means there must be at least two people in the vehicle for you to legally drive in that lane.
rules.quote: For example, "HOV 2" means there must be at least two people in the vehicle for you to legally drive in that lane.

rules.rule: During high inbound traffic hours (7–9 a.m.) and high outbound traffic (4–6 p.m.), the HOV lane is reserved for vehicles with two or more persons, buses with 2 or more occupants, motorcycles occupied by 1 person, and emergency vehicles.
rules.quote: During high inbound traffic hours (7–9 a.m.) and high outbound traffic (4–6 p.m.), the HOV lane is reserved for the exclusive use of: • Vehicles with two or more persons. (A baby in a car seat qualifies just like any other passenger.) • Buses with 2 or more occupants • Motorcycles occupied by 1 person • Emergency Vehicles

rules.rule: Drivers found in violation of the HOV lane are subject to a $50 fine and court costs.
rules.quote: Drivers found in violation of the HOV lane are subject to a $50 fine and court costs.

rules.rule: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder in the direction you will be moving, look behind to both sides again, check blind spots, and change gradually.
rules.quote: Check your rear view mirrors. • Signal your intention to change lanes. • Look over your shoulder in the direction you will be moving. • Look behind you to both sides again. • Check your blind spots.

rules.rule: When overtaking and passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction on a two-lane road in the USA, you should pass only to the left of the vehicle.
rules.quote: When overtaking and passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction on a two-lane road in the USA, you should pass only to the left of the vehicle.

rules.rule: Pass on the left at a safe distance and do not return to the right lane until safely clear of the overtaken vehicle.
rules.quote: Pass on the left at a safe distance and do not return to the right lane until safely clear of the overtaken vehicle.

rules.rule: It is not illegal in Tennessee to pass multiple vehicles, but it is not considered safe, and you should be able to return to the right lane before coming within 100 feet of the no-passing markings or any oncoming vehicles.
rules.quote: Can complete the pass of all vehicles and be safely returned to the right lane before coming within 100 feet of the no passing markings
extraQuotes: it is NOT SAFE to pass more than one vehicle at a time, although it is not illegal in Tennessee to pass multiple vehicles.

rules.rule: You may overtake and pass on the right only when the vehicle overtaken has signaled or is about to make a left turn, on an unobstructed roadway wide enough for two or more lanes in each direction, or on a one-way street sufficiently paved for two or more lanes.
rules.quote: The driver of a vehicle may overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle only under the following conditions: • When the vehicle overtaken has signaled to make or is about to make a left turn

rules.topic: Passing on the right, off pavement
rules.rule: Passing on the right is never permitted by driving off the pavement of the roadway.
rules.quote: Passing on the right is never permitted by driving off the pavement of the roadway.

rules.rule: Do not pass on the right using a bike lane or parking lane at any location, nor in the emergency lane within sight of a traffic light or stop sign.
rules.quote: Do NOT pass on the right using a bike lane or parking lane at any location, nor in the emergency lane within sight of a traffic light or stop sign.

rules.rule: You may not cross the center line to pass when there is an oncoming car, when approaching an intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel, whenever the solid yellow line is on your side, when approaching a hill or curve, or past a car stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk.
rules.quote: Do not pass when approaching any road-way intersection, railroad crossing, narrow bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
extraQuotes: Do not pass when approaching a hill or curve.

rules.rule: Do not pass a school bus or church bus when the flashing lights are operating and the stop arm is extended.
rules.quote: Do not pass a school bus or church bus when the flashing lights are operating and the stop arm is extended.

rules.rule: Do not pass on the right shoulder of the highway.
rules.quote: Do not pass on the right shoulder of the highway.

rules.rule: The end of a "no-passing zone" does not mean it is safe to pass; it means there is increased visibility ahead.
rules.quote: The end of a "no-passing zone" does not mean it is safe to pass. It means there is increased visibility ahead.

rules.rule: You are allowed to turn across the center line to enter or exit an alley, intersection, private road or driveway while in a no-passing zone.
rules.quote: You are allowed to turn across the center line if you are making a left turn into or coming out of an alley, intersection, private road or driveway while in the "no-passing zone".

rules.rule: When another driver passes you, stay in your lane, maintain your speed, and do not speed up to keep the other driver from passing.
rules.quote: Maintaining your speed. DO NOT speed up to keep the other driver from passing.

rules.rule: When passing and overtaking a bicyclist proceeding in the same direction you must leave a distance of not less than 3 feet, and maintain that clearance until safely past — it's the law.
rules.quote: leave at least a distance between you and the bicycle of not less than 3 feet. It's the law! Also be sure to maintain this clearance until safely past the overtaken bicycle.

rules.rule: Never attempt to pass between a bicyclist and oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road, and never pass a bicycle if the street is too narrow.
rules.quote: As a driver you should never attempt passing between a bicyclist and oncoming vehicles on a two-lane road.

rules.rule: It is illegal to exceed the posted speed limit even when passing other vehicles.
rules.quote: Remember, it is illegal to exceed the speed posted speed limit even when passing other vehicles.

rules.rule: When entering an interstate you must use the merging or acceleration lane to speed up and merge with fast-moving traffic, and it is your responsibility to yield the right-of-way to other cars on the interstate.
rules.quote: You must use the merging or acceleration lane to speed up and merge with fast-moving traffic already on the interstate.
extraQuotes: It is your responsibility to yield the right-of-way to other cars on the interstate.

rules.rule: A "lane added" sign means the on-ramp becomes a new lane and entering traffic does not need to merge immediately, while a "merge" sign means the traffic coming from the right must merge into the existing right lane.
rules.quote: The "lane added" sign means that there is a new right lane added to the interstate/roadway for the incoming traffic. The on-ramp becomes a new lane and the entering traffic does not need to merge immediately.

rules.rule: The left lane is for passing only, and if you are in the left lane and someone comes up behind you at a faster speed you should move one lane to your right.
rules.quote: If you are traveling in the left lane and someone comes up behind you at a faster speed, move one lane to your right.
extraQuotes: Left lane is for passing only.

rules.rule: Exit signs are usually placed at least one mile ahead of the exit turn-off.
rules.quote: Exit signs are usually placed at least one mile ahead of the exit turn-off.

rules.rule: The paved shoulder of the interstate should not be used for vehicular travel except for deceleration when marked for that purpose or for an emergency.
rules.quote: The paved shoulder of the interstate should not be used for vehicular travel except for deceleration when marked for this purpose or for an emergency.

rules.rule: It is illegal to park a motor vehicle, attended or unattended, upon the paved or unpaved portions of any entrance or exit ramp of any highway unless the vehicle is disabled.
rules.quote: It is illegal to park a motor vehicle, whether attended or unattended upon the paved or unpaved portions of any entrance or exit ramp of any highway unless the vehicle is disabled.

rules.rule: It is illegal to back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways and illegal to cross the median on the interstate; if you miss your exit you must proceed to the next exit.
rules.quote: It is also illegal to back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, you must proceed to the next exit. It is illegal to cross the median on the interstate.

rules.rule: At a diamond interchange the right turn entrance ramp is always encountered before crossing over or under the interstate, and the left turn entrance ramp always after.
rules.quote: (1) The RIGHT TURN entrance ramp will always be encountered BEFORE crossing over or under the interstate. (2) The LEFT TURN entrance ramp will always be encountered AFTER crossing over or under the interstate.

rules.rule: At a cloverleaf interchange all turns are right turns: to turn right take the right turn before the overpass, to turn left take the right turn just after the overpass.
rules.quote: At a cloverleaf interchange, all turns are right turns. To turn right, take the right turn before you get to the overpass. To turn left, take the right turn just after the overpass.

rules.rule: Parking on the shoulder of the interstate is prohibited except in cases of emergency.
rules.quote: Parking on the shoulder of the interstate is prohibited except in cases of emergency.

rules.rule: Walking on the interstate is both illegal and dangerous, and except in extreme emergencies you should remain in your disabled vehicle until help arrives.
rules.quote: Walking on the interstate is both illegal and dangerous. Except for extreme emergency cases, remain in your disabled vehicle until a State Trooper, other police officer, emergency service vehicle or a good Samaritan stops to offer assistance.

rules.rule: If involved in a crash on the interstate with no serious personal injuries or deaths and the vehicle is still drivable, Tennessee law allows you to pull the vehicle to the emergency lane and await a trooper.
rules.quote: If the vehicle is still drivable and there are NO SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURIES or deaths, you may pull the vehicle(s) to the emergency lane and await the arrival of a trooper or police officer to the crash scene.

rules.rule: Under Tennessee law you must not leave the scene of any type of crash, and while remaining at the scene you should not unnecessarily obstruct traffic.
rules.quote: Under Tennessee law, you must not leave the scene of any type of crash, and while remaining at the scene, you should not "unnecessarily obstruct traffic."

rules.rule: Dialing \*THP (\*847) on a wireless phone connects you at no charge to the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatcher.
rules.quote: you may use your wireless phone at no charge to directly connect with the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatch Center. Dial: * T H P (*847)

rules.rule: Never back a vehicle into any travel lane, with the exception of backing into a parallel parking space.
rules.quote: Never back a vehicle into any travel lane with the exception of backing into a parallel parking space.

rules.rule: It is illegal to back into an intersection from a driveway.
rules.quote: It is illegal to back into an intersection from a driveway.

rules.rule: It is illegal to back up on the interstate.
rules.quote: It is illegal to back up on the interstate.

rules.rule: Do not stop in the travel lanes for any reason; keep moving until you can safely pull your vehicle off the roadway.
rules.quote: Do not stop in the travel lanes for any reason (lost or confused about directions, vehicle breakdown, or letting out a passenger). Keep moving until you can safely pull your vehicle off the roadway.

rules.rule: If stopping at a curb, move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.
rules.quote: If stopping at a curb, move to within 18 inches of the curb for proper parking.

rules.rule: When parking adjacent to a roadway outside the city limits all four wheels must be off the pavement if possible, you must leave at least 18 feet of road width for other traffic, and your vehicle must be visible for at least 200 feet in either direction.
rules.quote: you must ensure that you leave at least 18 feet of road width for other traffic to pass your parked vehicle. Plus, your vehicle must be visible for at least 200 feet in either direction

rules.rule: It is against the law to leave the engine running in a parked unattended vehicle.
rules.quote: It is against the law to leave the engine running in a parked unattended vehicle.

rules.rule: Remove ignition keys from a parked and unattended vehicle.
rules.quote: Remove ignition keys from a parked and unattended vehicle.

rules.rule: A driver must look, signal and yield the right-of-way when coming out of any type of parking space, including parallel spaces.
rules.quote: A driver must look, signal and yield the right-of-way when coming out of any type of parking space, including parallel spaces.

rules.rule: Always set the parking brake when you park, leaving the vehicle in gear if manual or in park if automatic.
rules.quote: Always set the parking brake when you park. Leave the vehicle in gear if it has a manual transmission, or in park if it has an automatic transmission.

rules.rule: Double parking is prohibited by law.
rules.quote: Double parking is prohibited by law.

rules.rule: On a downhill with a curb, turn the front wheels toward the curb (right) and set the parking brake.
rules.quote: On a downhill with a curb: Turn the front wheels toward the curb (right) and set the parking brake.

rules.rule: On an uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb (left).
rules.quote: On an uphill with a curb: Turn the front wheels away from curb (left).

rules.rule: On a downhill or uphill without a curb, turn the front wheels toward the edge of the roadway (right).
rules.quote: On a downhill without a curb: Turn the front wheels toward the edge of the roadway (right).
extraQuotes: On an uphill without a curb: Turn the front wheels toward the edge of the roadway (right).

rules.rule: It is illegal to park in front of a driveway, on interstate ramps (unless disabled), within an intersection, within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, within a fire lane, within 20 feet of a crosswalk, within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side (75 feet on the other side), within 30 feet of a traffic control device, within 50 feet of a railroad crossing, on a sidewalk, on a bridge or in a tunnel, in a handicap space, double-parked, on an interstate shoulder, or where signs prohibit stopping or standing.
rules.quote: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant • Within a fire lane • Within 20 feet of a crosswalk or in the crosswalk marked area • Within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street or on the other side of the street within 75 feet of the fire station driveway • Within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or any other traffic control device • Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing

rules.rule: A white painted curb means stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers, yellow means stop only long enough to load or unload while staying with your car, and red means do not stop, stand or park under any condition.
rules.quote: 1. Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers. 2. Stop only long enough to load or unload. Stay with your car. 3. Do not stop, stand or park in this space under any condition.

rules.rule: When parallel parking, your rear bumper should be even with the bumper of the other parked car and your vehicle should not be any closer than two feet from the other vehicle.
rules.quote: Your rear bumper should be even with the bumper of the other parked car. Your vehicle should not be any closer than two feet from the other vehicle.

rules.rule: Begin backing very slowly, turning the steering wheel sharply to the right until the car is at about a 45-degree angle with the street.
rules.quote: turning the steering wheel sharply to the right until the car is at about a 45-degree angle with the street.

rules.rule: Upon completion of the parallel parking maneuver the vehicle should be no farther away from the curb than 18 inches.
rules.quote: the vehicle should be no farther away from the curb than 18 inches.

rules.rule: If you must leave your vehicle parked on a highway, park with all four wheels off the traveled portion if possible, raise the hood or tie a handkerchief to the left door handle or antenna, turn on emergency flashers, set the parking brake and lock the vehicle.
rules.quote: If you cannot move the vehicle off the highway, raise the hood or tie a handkerchief on the left door handle or antenna to warn other motorists of your stopped vehicle.

rules.rule: Improperly parking in a handicap-designated space is a misdemeanor punishable by a $100 fine and the vehicle could be towed.
rules.quote: you will be committing a misdemeanor punishable by a $100 dollar fine, and your vehicle could be subject to being towed.

rules.rule: Parking spaces marked with the handicap symbol may only be used by vehicles displaying a valid placard or plate and only when transporting the person to whom it was issued.
rules.quote: Parking spaces marked with this symbol are only to be used by vehicles displaying a valid placard or license plate with this symbol, and only when transporting the person who was issued the placard or plate.

rules.rule: The hazard or four-way flashing directional lights may be displayed during the hours of darkness when a vehicle is disabled or otherwise presents a traffic hazard.
rules.quote: The "hazard" or four-way flashing directional lights may be displayed during the hours of darkness when a vehicle is disabled or otherwise presents a traffic hazard.

rules.rule: When parking at night never leave your headlights on, and whenever you park on or along a highway at night leave your emergency and parking lights on.
rules.quote: Whenever you park on or along a highway at night, leave your emergency and parking lights on.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Under Public Chapter No. 412 (2019) it is illegal for a driver to hold a cellphone or mobile device with any part of their body, write/send/read text-based communication, reach for a device out of a seated restrained position, watch a video, or record or broadcast video.
rules.quote: (a) hold a cellphone or mobile device with any part of their body, (b) write, send, or read any text-based communication, (c) reach for a cellphone or mobile device in a manner that requires the driver to no longer be in a seated driving position or properly restrained by a seat belt, (d) watch a video or movie on a cellphone or mobile device, and (e) record or broadcast video on a cellphone or mobile device.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: You are not allowed to touch your phone in order to use GPS; you must find a safe place to pull over, stop, and then operate the phone or GPS.
rules.quote: You are not allowed to touch your phone in order to use GPS. If you need to access GPS or to use your phone, you must find a safe place to pull over such as in a parking lot, bring your vehicle to a full stop and operate your phone or GPS technology.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Texting while driving violations can result in a fine not to exceed fifty dollars and court costs not to exceed ten dollars.
rules.quote: Violations can result in a fine not to exceed Fifty Dollars, and court costs not to exceed Ten Dollars.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency medical persons and emergency management agency officers in the discharge of official duties are exempt from the texting law.
rules.quote: Law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency medical persons and emergency management agency officers when in the actual discharge of their official duties, are exempt from the provisions of the law.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Effective January 1, 2018 it is an offense for persons 18 or older to use a hand-held mobile phone while a vehicle is in motion in any marked school zone when a warning flasher is in operation, except in hands-free mode.
rules.quote: Effective January 1, 2018, it is an offense for persons 18 years or older to use a hand-held mobile phone while a motor vehicle is in motion in any marked school zone in this state, when a warning flasher or flashers are in operation. There is an exception if the phone is being used in hands free mode.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: The hands-free-mode exception does not apply to persons under eighteen and creates a delinquent act for those individuals.
rules.quote: This exception also does not apply to persons under eighteen (18) years of age and creates a delinquent act for these individuals.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: State law prohibits installing a video monitor or screen capable of displaying a television broadcast or video signal intended to display an image visible to the driver while the vehicle is in motion.
rules.quote: State law prohibits the installation of a video monitor or video screen capable of displaying a television broadcast or video signal that is intended to display an image visible to the driver of a vehicle while in motion.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Navigation or GPS devices, vehicle information system displays, and visual displays for the driver's view forward, behind and to the sides are not prohibited.
rules.quote: A navigation or global positioning device, a vehicle information system display, visual displays for the driver's view forward, behind and the sides of the vehicle are not prohibited.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Drivers should place the left hand at the 9 o'clock position and the right hand at the 3 o'clock position on the steering wheel.
rules.quote: drivers should place the left hand at the 9 o'clock position and the right hand at 3 o'clock position on the steering wheel. This position helps avoid injury from air bag deployment during an accident.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Your body should be about 10 to 12 inches back from the steering wheel with or without an air bag.
rules.quote: Your body should be about 10 to 12 inches back from the steering wheel with or without an air bag.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Head restraints should be adjusted to a level even with the back of the head and are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.
rules.quote: Properly adjust seat head restraints to a level even with the back of the head. Head restraints are designed to prevent whiplash if hit from behind.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Do not drive with the seat in a reclined or semi-reclined position, as it reduces both your vision and your ability to react.
rules.quote: DO NOT DRIVE WITH THE SEAT IN A RECLINED OR SEMI-RECLINED POSITION. This is dangerous and reduces both your vision and your ability to react to emergency situations.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Never turn the ignition to the lock position when the vehicle is in motion, because the steering wheel will lock and control will be lost.
rules.quote: never turn the ignition to the lock position when the vehicle is in motion The steering wheel will lock when trying to turn and the control of the vehicle will be lost.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: The Push-Pull steering method is recommended because it slows down turning movements and keeps both hands on the wheel through the entire maneuver.
rules.quote: The Push-Pull method is recommended because it slows down turning movements making for a smoother, safer turn. It also keeps both hands on the steering wheel through the entire maneuver.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: Never let the engine run in a closed garage and do not use a heater or air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed.
rules.quote: Never let the engine run in a closed garage • Do not use a heater/air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.
rules.quote: In normal daylight, vehicles are visible at twice the distance when headlights are on.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: If the tread does not come at least to Lincoln's head (2/32 inch) when a penny is inserted head first, the tire is illegal and unsafe and needs to be replaced.
rules.quote: If the tread does not come at least to Lincoln's head (2/32 inch), the tire is illegal and unsafe and you need it replaced.

rules.group: Distracted driving, phones and in-vehicle equipment
rules.rule: If your license indicates you must wear corrective lenses (Restriction Code 01) you must wear them at all times when driving or you could be fined and ticketed.
rules.quote: If your driver license indicates you must wear corrective lenses (Restriction Code 01) you must wear them at all times when driving. You could be fined and receive a ticket if stopped while driving without your glasses or contacts.

rules.rule: The basic rule for safe night driving is never outrun your headlights, and you must make sure your stopping distance is less than your sight distance.
rules.quote: The basic rule for safe night driving is this: NEVER OUTRUN YOUR HEADLIGHTS.
extraQuotes: Make sure your stopping distance is less than your sight distance.

rules.rule: Dim your lights when meeting or overtaking vehicles within 500 feet, always use low beams in cities and towns, and avoid blasting oncoming cars on curves or right turns.
rules.quote: Meeting or overtaking vehicles within 500 feet. • Driving in cities and towns always use your low beams • On curves or turns to the right avoid "blasting" an oncoming car with your high beams.

rules.rule: Avoid the glare of oncoming lights by watching the right edge of the road and using the white line or road edge as a steering guide, and avoid looking directly into oncoming headlights.
rules.quote: Avoid the glare of oncoming lights by watching the right edge of the road and using the white line or road edge as a steering guide.

rules.rule: Wet pavement can be as treacherous as icy pavement, so always reduce your speed in wet weather.
rules.quote: Wet pavement can be as treacherous as icy pavement, so always reduce your speed in wet weather.

rules.rule: The pavement is particularly treacherous when it first begins to rain, because dirt and oil mix with the water to create a greasy film.
rules.quote: The pavement is particularly treacherous when it first begins to rain. Accumulations of dirt and oil will mix with the water, and create a greasy film on the roadway.

rules.rule: Shade from trees or buildings can hide spots of ice on cold wet days, and bridges and overpasses tend to freeze before the rest of the road.
rules.quote: Bridges and overpasses can also hide spots of ice. They tend to freeze before the rest of the road does.

rules.rule: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, slow down gradually by letting up on the gas and don't slam on the brakes.
rules.quote: a. If you vehicle starts to hydroplane, slow down gradually by letting up on the gas. b. Don't slam on the brakes.

rules.rule: When hydroplaning occurs there is a loss of traction, stopping distances may be tripled and steering control may be reduced or lost.
rules.quote: When hydroplaning occurs there is a loss of the traction needed to steer and brake safely. d. Stopping distances may be tripled and steering control may be reduced or lost.

rules.rule: Hydroplaning is more common at higher speeds, although tires can hydroplane under certain conditions at any speed.
rules.quote: Hydroplaning is more common at higher speeds, although tires can hydroplane under certain conditions at ANY speed.

rules.rule: Skids are caused when the tires can no longer grip the road, and are caused by drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
rules.quote: Skids are caused when the tires can no longer grip the road. Skids are caused by drivers traveling too fast for conditions.

rules.rule: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay off the brake and turn the steering wheel in the direction you want your car to go, then correct back the other way as it straightens.
rules.quote: b. Steer. Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want your car to go.

rules.rule: If your wheels go off the paved roadway, lift off the gas without suddenly braking, hold the wheel firmly without jerking it back, brake lightly and briefly, and do not steer back onto the pavement until there are no cars in your immediate vicinity.
rules.quote: 5. Do NOT attempt to steer back onto the pavement until there are no cars in your immediate vicinity.

rules.rule: If a driver knowingly ignores clearly visible and adequate flood warning signs or barricades and drives into a flooded road area, the driver can be charged with reckless driving and be responsible for the cost of the rescue.
rules.quote: the driver can be charged with reckless driving. The driver can also be responsible for the restitution of funds for the cost of your rescue.

rules.rule: As little as six to twelve inches of water may cause you to lose control of your vehicle and two feet of water will carry most cars downstream.
rules.quote: As little as six to twelve inches of water may cause you to lose control of your vehicle and two feet of water will carry most cars downstream.

rules.rule: Never drive through floodwaters or on flooded roads, and if your vehicle stalls, leave it immediately and seek higher ground.
rules.quote: NEVER drive through floodwaters or on flooded roads. If your vehicle stalls, leave it immediately and seek higher ground.

rules.rule: If you spot a tornado do not try to outrun it; get out of the car, find shelter in a ditch or low-lying area and lie face down.
rules.quote: If you spot a tornado, DON'T try to outrun it. Get out of the car, find shelter in a ditch or low-lying area and lie face down to protect yourself from flying debris.

rules.rule: To gain more control over a vehicle in a strong wind, slow down; when a truck or bus passes you on the left, move as far as possible to the right of your lane and slow down.
rules.quote: a. To gain more control over vehicles in a strong wind, slow down.

rules.rule: The three big errors of most drivers in snow and ice are to over-power and spin the wheels, over-brake and slide the wheels, and over-steer and skid the wheels.
rules.quote: To over-power and spin the wheels • To over-brake and slide the wheels • To over-steer and skid the wheels

rules.rule: Clear snow, ice or frost from all windows before driving.
rules.quote: Clear snow, ice or frost from ALL windows before driving.

rules.rule: Continuous hard braking on snow and ice can result in the locking of the front brakes causing a loss of steering, and you should not pump the brake pedal but apply steady pressure.
rules.quote: Continuous hard braking on snow and ice can result in the locking of the front brakes causing a loss of steering.
extraQuotes: Do NOT pump the brake pedal, just apply steady pressure.

rules.rule: In hailstorms or sleet, find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge.
rules.quote: Hailstorms/Sleet – find shelter by driving under an overpass or bridge.

rules.rule: In avoiding a collision, drivers have three options: stop, turn, or speed up.
rules.quote: In avoiding a collision, drivers have three options: 1. Stop 2. Turn 3. Speed Up

rules.rule: With ABS, press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing firmly; do not let up even if the pedal pushes back.
rules.quote: Press on the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep pressing on it firmly.

rules.rule: Without ABS, apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking them; if the brakes lock up, quickly let up on the pedal and push down again once the skid stops.
rules.quote: If the brakes lock-up, you will feel the vehicle start to skid. Quickly let up on the brake pedal.
extraQuotes: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking them.

rules.rule: If a collision with an animal seems inevitable, don't swerve to avoid the animal; keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway.
rules.quote: If a collision seems inevitable, don't swerve to avoid the animal; your risk of personal injury may be greater if you do. Keep your vehicle under control and on the roadway when you hit the animal.

rules.rule: Report the crash to the police if it involves a large animal such as a deer or farm animal.
rules.quote: Report the crash to the police if it involves a large animal such as a deer or farm animal.

rules.rule: The liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour, and this rate cannot be increased by coffee, exercise, a cold shower or anything else — only time can sober a person.
rules.quote: the liver can only oxidize about one drink per hour. Contrary to popular belief, this rate cannot be increased by drinking coffee, exercising, taking a cold shower or anything else. Only time can sober a person who's been drinking.

rules.rule: Blood Alcohol Concentration is a measurement of the percentage of alcohol in the blood, and the higher the BAC number the more impaired a person is.
rules.quote: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is a measurement of the percentage of alcohol in the blood. The higher the BAC number, the more impaired a person is.

rules.rule: In Tennessee, .08 is the level of intoxication which is always illegal.
rules.quote: In most states, including Tennessee, .08 is the level of intoxication which is always illegal.

rules.rule: In Tennessee it is unlawful to drive or be in physical control of a motor vehicle on any public street, highway, road or alley, or on the premises of any shopping center, trailer park, apartment complex, or any place frequented by the public, while under the influence of any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic drug or stimulating drug, or while the alcohol concentration of the blood or breath is .08 percent or higher.
rules.quote: 1. Under the influence of any intoxicant, marijuana, narcotic drug or drugs producing stimulating effects on the central nervous system; or 2. While the alcohol concentration of the operator's blood or breath is .08 percent or higher.

rules.rule: A driver can register a BAC of .00 percent and still be convicted of a DUI, and a BAC below .08 percent does not clear a driver.
rules.quote: A driver can register a BAC of .00 percent and still be convicted of a DUI. The level of BAC does not clear a driver when it is below .08 percent.

rules.rule: Just because a drug is prescribed by law, this is no defense for driving under the influence of it.
rules.quote: Just because a drug is prescribed, by law, this is NO defense for driving under the influence of it.

rules.rule: Driving under the influence of drugs — even prescription drugs — carries the same penalties as for alcohol.
rules.quote: driving while under the influence of drugs—even prescription drugs—carries the same penalties as for alcohol.

rules.rule: By law, when you drive in Tennessee you have given your consent to be tested to determine the alcohol or drug content of your blood at the request of a law enforcement officer with reasonable grounds.
rules.quote: By law, when you drive in Tennessee, you have given your consent to be tested to determine the alcohol or drug content of your blood. This test must be administered at the request of a law enforcement officer who has reasonable grounds to believe you have been driving under the influence of an intoxicant or drug.

rules.rule: If you are placed under arrest and refuse the test, it will likely result in the suspension by the court of your driving privileges for twelve months.
rules.quote: If you are placed under arrest and a law enforcement officer asks you to take the test and you refuse, it will likely result in the suspension by the court of your driving privileges for twelve (12) months.

rules.rule: The No Refusal law, passed in 2012, allows law enforcement to seek search warrants for blood samples in cases involving suspected impaired drivers.
rules.quote: The No Refusal law was passed in 2012 and allows law enforcement officials to seek search warrants for blood samples in cases involving suspected impaired drivers.

rules.rule: A first DUI conviction carries 48 hours jail (7 days if BAC is 0.20% or more), a $350–$1,500 fine, and 1 year license revocation.
rules.quote: 48 hours (7 days if BAC is 0.20% or more)

rules.rule: A second DUI conviction carries 45 days to 11 months 29 days jail, a $600–$3,500 fine, 2 years revocation, and the vehicle is subject to seizure and forfeiture.
rules.quote: Vehicle is subject to seizure and forfeiture
extraQuotes: 45 days – 11 months, 29 days

rules.rule: A third DUI conviction carries 120 days to 11 months 29 days jail, a $1,100–$10,000 fine, 3–10 years revocation, and vehicle seizure and forfeiture.
rules.quote: 120 days – 11 months, 29 days

rules.rule: A fourth or subsequent DUI conviction is a Class E felony carrying 150 days to the maximum allowable for a Class E felony, a $3,000–$15,000 fine, and 5 years to indefinite revocation.
rules.quote: 4th or subsequent Conviction (is a Class E felony)
extraQuotes: 150 days – max allowable for a Class E felony

rules.rule: A person whose license is revoked for DUI and who applies for a photo identification license must have the ID indicate that the person is a DUI offender.
rules.quote: the department is required to indicate on the ID that the person is a DUI offender.

rules.rule: A DUI conviction requires, as a condition of probation, litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts while wearing a vest displaying "I am a DRUNK DRIVER."
rules.quote: A DUI conviction also requires as a condition of probation, litter pick-up for three eight-hour shifts. While removing litter, the offender has to wear a vest or other clothing displaying the message, "I am a DRUNK DRIVER."

rules.rule: Operating a vehicle under the influence and being involved in a crash resulting in death may be charged as vehicular homicide, with fines and prison.
rules.quote: you may be charged with vehicular homicide. If convicted, you may be fined and sentenced to prison.

rules.rule: Operating a vehicle under the influence and being involved in a crash resulting in injury may be charged as aggravated assault.
rules.quote: you may be charged with aggravated assault. If convicted, you may be fined and sentenced to prison.

rules.rule: Violating DUI laws while accompanied by a child under 18 carries a mandatory minimum jail sentence of 30 days and a mandatory minimum fine of $1,000, added on to any other penalties.
rules.quote: There is a mandatory minimum jail sentence of 30 days, and a mandatory minimum fine of $1,000. Both of these child-related penalties are added onto any other incarceration, penalty and fines.

rules.rule: If a child suffers serious bodily injury in a DUI the violation is a Class D felony, and if the child dies it is a Class C felony of especially aggravated child endangerment.
rules.quote: If the child suffers serious bodily injury, the violation is a Class D felony, and if the child dies, it is a Class C felony of especially aggravated child endangerment.

rules.rule: The driver's vehicle will be seized if he or she has two DUI convictions within five years and both events happened after January 1997.
rules.quote: The driver's vehicle will be seized if he/she has two DUI convictions within five years AND both events happened after January 1997.

rules.rule: The ignition interlock restriction can be from six months to one year for a first offense, up to three years for a second offense and up to 10 years for third and subsequent offenses.
rules.quote: The restriction can be from six months to one year for a first offense, up to three years for a second offense and up to 10 years for third and subsequent offenses

rules.rule: A person with 2 DUIs in a five-year period must operate a motor vehicle with the ignition interlock device for six months after reinstatement of driving privileges.
rules.quote: a person with 2 DUIs in a five year period MUST operate a motor vehicle with the ignition interlock device for six months after reinstatement of driving privileges.

rules.rule: A person 18, 19 or 20 convicted of purchasing, attempting to purchase, or possessing any alcoholic beverage loses the privilege to drive for one year, and two years for a second occurrence, whether or not driving was involved.
rules.quote: you will lose your privilege to drive for one year. If it happens a second time you will lose your license for two years. The law applies to any alcohol-related conviction, whether or not you were driving or even in a vehicle.

rules.rule: A person between 13 and 17 found to have possessed, consumed or sold alcohol or drugs has driving privileges suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer; a second conviction is two years or until age 18, whichever is longer.
rules.quote: If you have a second conviction, the suspension is for two years or until age 18, whichever is longer.
extraQuotes: your driving privilege will be suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer

rules.rule: A person at least 16 but not yet 21 driving with a BAC of .02 percent, under the influence of alcohol, or under the influence of any other intoxicant will be convicted of underage driving while impaired, losing the license for one year with a $250 fine and sometimes public service work.
rules.quote: Penalties for this conviction are: losing your license for one year, a fine of $250 and sometimes, includes public service work.
extraQuotes: A person who is at least 16, but is not yet 21 years old, and who is found: (1) driving with a BAC of .02 percent

rules.rule: Alcohol reduces the ability to see clearly at night by more than half, and side vision is reduced by about 30 percent at .05 percent BAC.
rules.quote: It reduces the ability to see clearly at night by more than half
extraQuotes: Side vision is reduced by about 30 percent at .05 percent BAC.

rules.rule: Reaction and coordination are impaired by alcohol consumption as low as .02 percent BAC.
rules.quote: Reaction and coordination are impaired by alcohol consumption as low as .02 percent BAC.

rules.rule: Research has proven that driving skills, good judgment and vision are greatly impaired at BAC levels as low as .03 and .04 percent, and all people at the .10 percent level are definitely too impaired to drive safely.
rules.quote: ALL people at the .10 percent level are definitely too impaired to drive safely. Research has proven that driving skills, good judgment and vision are greatly impaired at BAC levels as low as .03 and .04 percent

rules.rule: With a BAC of .10 percent you are seven times more likely to cause a crash, at .15 percent 25 times, and at .17 percent 50 times.
rules.quote: With a BAC of .10 percent, you are seven times more likely to cause a crash than if you were sober. As your BAC increases to .15 percent, your chances of causing a traffic crash increase to 25 times. At .17 percent BAC, you are 50 times more likely to cause a crash.

rules.rule: Alcohol, in any concentration, is a depressant, not a stimulant.
rules.quote: Alcohol, in any concentration, is a depressant, not a stimulant.

rules.rule: The amount of alcohol in one 12-ounce bottle of beer is about equal to that in a 1-ounce shot of whiskey.
rules.quote: The amount of alcohol in one (12 ounce) bottle of beer is about equal to that in a (1 ounce) shot of whiskey.

rules.rule: The first thing affected after drinking alcohol is a person's judgment.
rules.quote: The first thing affected after drinking alcohol is a person's judgment.

rules.rule: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink and about three hours to cancel the intoxicating effects of three drinks.
rules.quote: It takes about one hour to cancel the effects of one drink. It takes about three hours to cancel the intoxicating effects of three drinks.

rules.rule: Because the eyes provide almost 90 percent of the information used in driving, any restriction in vision can cause disastrous results.
rules.quote: Because the eyes provide almost 90 percent of the information used in driving, any restriction in vision can cause disastrous results.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: A Tennessee driver license may be revoked or suspended for DUI (including implied-consent refusal), unlawful use of a license, disqualifying mental or physical difficulties, leaving the scene of an injury or fatal crash, perjury, a felony involving a vehicle, evading arrest, vehicular homicide, two reckless driving violations within 12 months, drag racing, habitual moving violations, unsatisfied judgments, underage alcohol possession, child support non-compliance, gas drive-off, failure to show insurance, or possession of five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle.
rules.quote: 17. Possession by a driver of five or more grams of methamphetamine in a vehicle.
extraQuotes: 9. Two reckless driving violations within 12 months.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Persons under 18 may lose driving privileges for any drug or alcohol offense whether or not it occurred while driving, dropping out of school, failure to make satisfactory progress, or possession or carrying weapons on school property.
rules.quote: Convictions of any drug or alcohol offense, whether or not the offense occurred while driving; • Dropping out of school
extraQuotes: Possession or carrying weapons on school property.
Failure to make satisfactory progress in school

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Dropping out of school is defined as having 10 consecutive or 15 total days in a semester of unexcused absences.
rules.quote: Dropping out of school (which is defined as having 10 consecutive or 15 total days in a semester of unexcused absences)

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Failure to make satisfactory progress in school generally means failing to pass three subjects per grading period.
rules.quote: Failure to make satisfactory progress in school (which, in general, means passing three subjects per grading period)

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: A suspended or revoked license must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days of the suspension or revocation.
rules.quote: Whenever a driver license is suspended or revoked, it must be turned in to the Department of Safety within 20 days of the suspension or revocation.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Failure to surrender your license means a $75 fine in addition to any other fines and costs owed.
rules.quote: Failure to surrender your license means that you will be fined $75 in addition to any other fines and costs you may owe.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Adult drivers 18 or older who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.
rules.quote: Adult drivers (18 years of age or older) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: An advisory letter is mailed to any adult licensee having 6 to 11 points on their driving record within any 12 months.
rules.quote: an advisory letter is mailed to any licensee having 6 to 11 points on his/her driving record within any 12 months.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Juvenile drivers under 18 who accumulate 6 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.
rules.quote: Juvenile drivers (less than 18 years of age) who accumulate 6 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: An advisory letter is mailed to any juvenile licensee having 1 to 5 points on their driving record within any 12 months.
rules.quote: an advisory letter is mailed to any licensee having 1 to 5 points on his/her driving record within any 12 months.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Drivers may attend a Defensive Driving Course to avoid or reduce suspension, but this option is only available once in any five-year period.
rules.quote: the Defensive Driving Course option is only available once in any five-year period.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Driving while your license is suspended will result in extension of the suspension period and could also result in criminal prosecution.
rules.quote: DRIVING WHILE YOUR LICENSE IS SUSPENDED WILL RESULT IN THE EXTENSION OF THE SUSPENSION PERIOD AND COULD ALSO RESULT IN CRIMINAL PROSECUTION.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Upon completion of the suspension time you must pay reinstatement fees and submit proof of liability insurance/financial responsibility, with SR-22 insurance required for adult drivers.
rules.quote: you must pay the appropriate reinstatement fees and submit proof of liability insurance/financial responsibility (SR-22 insurance is required for adult drivers)

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: A restricted license is not an option for drivers with a prior conviction of DUI or adult driving while impaired within 10 years, vehicular homicide as a result of intoxication, aggravated vehicular homicide, or vehicular assault.
rules.quote: DUI or adult driving while impaired within 10 years; • Vehicular Homicide as the latest result of intoxication; • Aggravated Vehicular Homicide; • Vehicular Assault.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: After the first year of a two-year revocation, drivers may apply for a restricted license if they install an ignition interlock device for the remaining period of revocation.
rules.quote: After the first year of a two-year revocation, drivers may apply for a restricted driver license if they install an ignition interlock device on the motor vehicle for the remaining period of revocation.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Applicants for most restricted licenses must submit two copies of the court order and proof of SR-22 insurance and pay required fees.
rules.quote: these applicants must submit two (2) copies of the court order and proof of car insurance/financial responsibility (SR-22 from their insurance company) and pass appropriate tests and pay the required fees.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: A driver whose ability to drive is affected by a physical or mental disorder must submit a medical report from a medical doctor within thirty days of notification.
rules.quote: the driver will be required to submit (within thirty (30) days of notification) a medical report from a medical doctor.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Drivers who lose consciousness or control due to epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or other conditions must be suspended and remain lapse free for a minimum of six months before being eligible for reinstatement.
rules.quote: Drivers who lose consciousness or control due to epilepsy, cardiac syncope, diabetes or other conditions must be suspended and remain lapse free for a minimum of six (6) months before being eligible for license reinstatement.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: In Tennessee you may drive if you are under the care of a doctor and have been seizure free for a minimum of six months.
rules.quote: In Tennessee, you may drive if you are under the care of a doctor and have been seizure free for a minimum of six months.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: The Financial Responsibility Law requires drivers to produce evidence of financial responsibility when charged with any violation or when involved in a motor vehicle crash, without regard to apparent or actual fault.
rules.quote: the Financial Responsibility Law requires drivers to produce evidence of financial responsibility. This is required when charged with any violation or when involved in a motor vehicle crash without regard to apparent or actual fault.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Collision insurance is not required by Tennessee law.
rules.quote: Although collision insurance is not required by Tennessee law, the Financial Responsibility Law requires drivers to produce evidence of financial responsibility.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Liability insurance covers damages you cause to other persons, collision insurance covers damages to your own vehicle, and uninsured motorist insurance covers damages uninsured persons cause.
rules.quote: Liability insurance provides coverage for damages you cause to other persons. • Collision insurance provides coverage for damages sustained by your vehicle. • Uninsured motorist insurance provides for coverage for the damages uninsured persons cause.

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: Drivers must immediately notify police of any crash involving death, injury, or property damage over fifty dollars.
rules.quote: Drivers must immediately notify the local police department if the crash occurs within a municipality, otherwise to the County Sheriff's office or the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol, of any crash involving death, injury or property damage over fifty dollars ($50).

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: A reportable crash is any crash in this state in which any person is killed or injured, or in which damage to the property of any one person, including oneself, is in excess of four hundred dollars.
rules.quote: These include any crash within this state in which any person is killed or injured, or in which damage to the property of any one person, including oneself, is in excess of four hundred dollars ($400).

rules.group: Driving responsibility — points, suspension, insurance, crashes
rules.rule: The operator and/or owner of a vehicle involved in a reportable crash must file an Owner/Driver Report with the Department of Safety within 20 days, regardless of who is to blame.
